blasons.D'azur semé de billettes d'or, au lion d: Azure, semé of billets or, overall a lion of the same.
blasons.D'azur, semé de billettes d'or, au lion: Azure, semé of billets or, a lion crowned of the second, armed and langued gules.
blasons.Écartelé : I d'azur semé de billettes d': Quarterly: I, azure, semé of billets or, a lion crowned of the same, armed and langued gules (Nassau); II, or, a lion rampant guardant, armed, langued and crowned azure (Katzenelnbogen); III, gules, a fess argent (Vianden); IV, gules, two lions passant guardant or, armed, langued and crowned azure (Diez).
blasons.Écartelé : I d'azur semé de billettes, a: Quarterly: I, azure, semé of billets, overall a lion or, armed and langued gules (Nassau); II, or, a lion rampant guardant gules, armed, crowned and langued azure (Katzenelnbogen); III, gules, a fess argent (Vianden); IV, gules, two lions passant in pale (Diez); overall a quartering: I and IV, gules, a bend or (Châlon), II and III, or, a hunting horn azure, banded and stringed gules (Orange); overall an escutcheon of five points or equipollent to four azure (Geneva).

Quarterly: I, azure, semé of billets, a lion or, armed and langued gules (Nassau); II, or, a lion rampant guardant gules, armed, crowned and langued azure (Katzenelnbogen); III, gules, a fess argent (Vianden); IV, gules, two lions passant in pale (Diez); overall, quarterly Châlon and Orange, with the escutcheon of Geneva; an escutcheon sable, a fess argent in chief (Marquess of Flushing and Veere); an escutcheon gules, a fess bretessed and counter-bretessed argent in base (Buren).

Quarterly: I, azure, semé of billets, a lion or, armed and langued gules (Nassau); II, or, a lion rampant guardant gules, armed, crowned and langued azure (Katzenelnbogen); III, gules, a fess argent (Vianden); IV, gules, two lions passant in pale (Diez); V, argent, a stag passant gules (Spiegelberg); VI, argent, a fess sable accompanied in chief by two tufts of rushes vert (Liesveld); overall, a cross of the Teutonic Order.

Quarterly: I, azure, semé of billets, a lion or, armed and langued gules (Nassau); II, or, a lion rampant guardant gules (Katzenelnbogen); III, gules, a fess argent (Vianden); IV, gules, two lions passant in pale (Diez); V, argent, a stag passant gules (Spiegelberg); VI, argent, a fess sable accompanied in chief by two tufts of rushes vert (Liesveld); overall, quarterly Châlon and Orange, with Geneva, Moers (or, a chevron sable) and an escutcheon of Breda (gules, a fess bretessed and counter-bretessed argent).
blasons.D'azur semé de billettes d'or, chargé d': Azure, semé of billets or, charged with a lion crowned or, armed and langued gules, holding a sheaf of seven arrows argent, pointed and fletched or, and a sword argent hilted or.
blasons.Burelé de dix pièces d'argent et d'azur: Barry of ten argent and azure, a lion gules with forked tail in saltire, armed, langued and crowned or, the lion's shoulder charged with an escutcheon azure, semé of billets or, a lion crowned of the second, armed and langued gules (Nassau).
blasons.D'azur, à la croix pattée, au pied fiché: Azure, a cross pattée with a fitched foot or
blasons.Écartelé en 1 et 4, d'or à deux fasces d: Quarterly: 1 and 4, or, two fesses gules (Oldenburg); 2 and 3, azure, a cross pattée with a fitched foot or (Delmenhorst)
blasons.Écartelé : à la croix pattée d'argent bo: Quarterly, by a cross pattée argent fimbriated gules, the Dannebrog, with in I, or, nine hearts gules in three pales, three lions passant azure, armed and langued gules, crowned of the field, overall (Denmark); in II, azure, three crowns or (Sweden Modern); in III, gules, a lion crowned or, holding in its paws a Danish axe argent, hafted of the second (Norway Ancient); in IV, gules, a dragon or (Kingdom of the Vandals); overall, quarterly: 1 and 4, or, two lions passant azure, armed and langued gules (Schleswig); 2 and 3, gules, a nettle leaf argent (Holstein); over all of that, or, two fesses gules (Oldenburg)

Quarterly, by a cross pattée argent fimbriated gules, the Dannebrog, with in I, or, nine hearts gules in three pales, three lions passant azure, armed and langued gules, crowned of the field, overall (Denmark); in II, gules, a lion crowned or, holding in its paws a Danish axe argent, hafted of the second (Norway Ancient); in III, azure, three crowns or (Sweden Modern); in IV, or, a lion passant azure above nine hearts gules set 5 and 4 (Kingdom of the Goths); overall, quarterly: 1, or, two lions passant azure, armed and langued gules (Schleswig); 2, gules, a nettle leaf argent (Holstein); 3, gules, a swan argent, beaked, membered and gorged with a crown or (Stormarn); 4, or, two fesses gules (Oldenburg)

Quarterly, by a cross pattée argent fimbriated gules, the Dannebrog, with in I, or, nine hearts gules in three pales, three lions passant azure, armed and langued gules, crowned of the field, overall (Denmark); in II, gules, a lion crowned or, holding in its paws a Danish axe argent, hafted of the second (Norway Ancient); in III, or, a lion passant azure above nine hearts gules set 5 and 4 (Kingdom of the Goths); in IV, gules, a dragon or (Kingdom of the Vandals); in V, azure, three crowns or (Sweden Modern); in VI, gules, the Paschal Lamb argent, bearing a staff with a crosslet or set bend-sinisterwise, from which hangs a banner also argent charged with a cross gules (Gotland Ancient); in VII, or, two lions passant azure, armed and langued gules (Schleswig); in VIII, gules, a cod argent surmounted by a crown or (Iceland); in IX, gules, a nettle leaf argent (Holstein); in X, gules, a swan argent, beaked, membered and gorged with a crown or (Stormarn); in XI, or, two fesses gules (Oldenburg); in XII, azure, a cross pattée with a fitched foot or (Delmenhorst); overall, gules, a horseman or armed argent (Dithmarschen)

Quarterly, by a cross pattée argent fimbriated gules, the Dannebrog, with in I, or, nine hearts gules in three pales, three lions passant azure, armed and langued gules, crowned of the field, overall (Denmark); in II, gules, a lion crowned or, holding in its paws a Danish axe argent, hafted of the second (Norway Ancient); in III, per fess azure, three crowns or (Sweden Modern) and or, two lions passant azure, armed and langued gules (Schleswig); in IV, per fess or, a lion passant azure above nine hearts gules set 5 and 4 (Kingdom of the Goths) and gules, a dragon or (Kingdom of the Vandals); overall, per pale gules, a nettle leaf argent (Holstein) and gules, a swan argent, beaked, membered and gorged with a crown or (Stormarn), enté en point gules, a horseman armed argent (Dithmarschen); over all of that, per pale or, two fesses gules (Oldenburg) and azure, a cross pattée with a fitched foot or (Delmenhorst)

Quarterly, by a cross pattée argent fimbriated gules, the Dannebrog, with in I, or, nine hearts gules in three pales, three lions passant azure, armed and langued gules, crowned of the field, overall (Denmark); in II, or, two lions passant azure, armed and langued gules (Schleswig); in III, per fess: A, azure, three crowns or (Sweden Modern), and B, per fess gules, a cod skin argent held in pale by a crossbar sable, the whole crowned or, and azure, a ram passant argent langued gules and armed or (Faroe Islands), and azure, a polar bear argent armed of the first (Greenland); in IV, per fess or, a lion passant azure above nine hearts gules set 5 and 4 (Kingdom of the Goths) and gules, a dragon or (Kingdom of the Vandals); overall, quarterly: 1, gules, a nettle leaf argent (Holstein); 2, gules, a swan argent, beaked, membered and gorged with a crown or (Stormarn); 3, gules, a horseman armed argent (Dithmarschen); 4, gules, a horse's head couped or (Lauenburg); over all of that, per pale or, two fesses gules (Oldenburg) and azure, a cross pattée with a fitched foot or (Delmenhorst)

Quarterly, by a cross pattée argent fimbriated gules, the Dannebrog, with in I, or, nine hearts gules in three pales, three lions passant azure, armed and langued gules, crowned of the field, overall (Denmark); in II, or, two lions passant azure, armed and langued gules (Schleswig); in III, per fess: 1, azure, three crowns or (Sweden Modern), and 2, per pale gules, a cod skin argent held in pale by a crossbar sable, the whole crowned or (Iceland Ancient), and per fess azure, a ram passant argent langued gules and armed or, and azure, a polar bear passant argent armed of the first; in IV, per fess or, a lion passant azure above nine hearts gules set 5 and 4 (Kingdom of the Goths) and gules, a dragon or (Kingdom of the Vandals); overall, quarterly: 1, gules, a nettle leaf argent (Holstein); 2, gules, a swan argent, beaked, membered and gorged with a crown or (Stormarn); 3, gules, a horseman armed argent (Dithmarschen); 4, gules, a horse's head couped or (Lauenburg); over all of that, per pale or, two fesses gules (Oldenburg) and azure, a cross pattée with a fitched foot or (Delmenhorst)

Quarterly, by a cross pattée argent fimbriated gules, the Dannebrog, with in 1, or, nine hearts gules in three pales, three lions passant azure, armed and langued gules, crowned of the field, overall (Denmark); in 2, or, two lions passant azure, armed and langued gules (Schleswig); in 3, per fess: A, azure, three crowns or (Sweden Modern), and B, per pale azure, an eagle argent with its helm in profile (Iceland Modern), and per fess azure, a ram passant argent langued gules and armed or, and azure, a polar bear passant argent armed of the first; in 4, per fess or, a lion passant azure above nine hearts gules set 5 and 4 (Kingdom of the Goths) and gules, a dragon or (Kingdom of the Vandals); overall, quarterly: 1, gules, a nettle leaf argent (Holstein); 2, gules, a swan argent, beaked, membered and gorged with a crown or (Stormarn); 3, gules, a horseman armed argent (Dithmarschen); 4, gules, a horse's head couped or (Lauenburg); over all of that, per pale or, two fesses gules (Oldenburg) and azure, a cross pattée with a fitched foot or (Delmenhorst)
blasons.Ecartelé : à la croix d'argent bordée de: Quarterly, by a cross argent fimbriated gules, the Dannebrog, with in 1 and 4, or, nine hearts gules in three pales, three lions passant azure, armed and langued gules, crowned of the field, overall (Denmark Modern); in 2, or, two lions passant azure, armed and langued gules (Schleswig); in 3, per fess azure, three crowns or (Sweden Modern), and per pale, dexter, azure, a ram passant argent, langued gules, armed and horned or (Faroe Islands), and sinister, a polar bear argent armed and langued of the same (Greenland); overall, or, two fesses gules (Oldenburg)
blasons.Ecartelé : en 1 et 4, d'or, à neuf cœurs: Quarterly: 1 and 4, or, nine hearts gules, in three pales, three lions passant azure, armed and langued gules, crowned of the field, over all (Denmark); 2 and 3, gules, a lion rampant or, with three stars of the same in chief (Monpezat)
blasons.Ecartelé : 1, de gueules, au lion couron: Quarterly: 1, gules, a lion crowned or, holding in its paws a Danish axe argent, hafted of the second (Norway Ancient); 2, or, two lions passant azure, armed and langued gules (Schleswig); 3, gules, a nettle leaf argent (Holstein); 4, gules, a swan argent, beaked, membered and gorged with a crown or (Stormarn); enté en point gules, a horseman armed argent (Dithmarschen); overall, quarterly or, two fesses gules (Oldenburg) and azure, a cross pattée with a fitched foot or (Delmenhorst)
blasons.Écartelé : à la croix pattée d'or, qui e: Quarterly: a cross formy or, which is the Cross of Saint Eric, between in 1 and 4, azure, three crowns or (modern Sweden), in 2 and 3, azure, three bends sinister wavy argent, a crowned lion or over all (ancient Sweden); overall, quarterly: 1, gules, a crowned lion or, holding in its paws a Danish axe argent, hafted of the second (ancient Norway); 2, or, two lions passant azure, armed and langued gules (Schleswig); 3, gules, a nettle leaf argent (Holstein); 4, gules, a swan argent, beaked, membered and gorged with a crown or (Stormarn; enté in base gules, an armed horseman argent (Dithmarschen); over all of all, quarterly or, two bars gules (Oldenburg) and azure, a cross formy fitched or (Delmenhorst)
blasons.Au pairle patté d'or, cantonné en chef d: A pall formy or, between in chief azure, three crowns or (modern Sweden), to dexter gules, a crowned lion or, holding in its paws a halberd argent, hafted of the second, and to sinister azure, three bends sinister wavy argent, a crowned lion or over all (ancient Sweden), overall, quarterly: 1, gules, a nettle leaf argent (Holstein); 2, or, two lions passant azure, armed and langued gules (Schleswig); 3, gules, a swan argent, beaked, membered and gorged with a crown or (Stormarn); 4, gules, an armed horseman argent (Dithmarschen); over all of all, quarterly or, two bars gules (Oldenburg) and azure, a cross formy fitched or (Delmenhorst)
blasons.Accolé : D'or à l'aigle bicéphale de sab: Accolé: Or, a double-headed eagle sable, beaked and membered or, langued gules, each head surmounted by a closed crown of the field, the eagle in turn surmounted by a third closed crown of the field, holding a sceptre of the field in the dexter talon and an orb azure banded or in the sinister talon; the eagle charged at the breast with an escutcheon gules showing Saint George striking down the Dragon, on his charger argent, contourné (for Muscovy); and per pale of one and per fess of two: 1, gules, a crowned lion or, holding in its paws a Danish axe argent, hafted of the second (for ancient Norway); 2, gules, a nettle leaf argent (for Holstein); 3, gules, a swan argent, beaked, membered and gorged with a crown or (for Stormarn); 4, gules, an armed horseman argent (for Dithmarschen); 5, or, two bars gules (for Oldenburg); 6, per fess azure, a cross formy fitched or (for Delmenhorst) and or; overall: or, two lions passant azure, armed and langued gules (for Schleswig)
blasons.D'or à l'aigle bicéphale de sable, becqu: Or, a double-headed eagle sable, beaked and membered or, langued gules, each head surmounted by a closed crown of the field, the eagle surmounted by a third closed crown of the field, holding a sceptre of the field in the dexter talon and an orb azure banded or in the sinister talon; the eagle charged at the breast with an escutcheon gules showing Saint George striking down the dragon, on his charger argent (for Muscovy)
blasons.Parties au premier d'or à l'aigle impéri: Per pale, first, or, the imperial eagle of Russia charged on the breast with the quarterly of Leuchtenberg, of Eichstätt, of vert a sword argent hilted or with seven stars of the last, of Beauharnais, overall azure, a closed crown or, the quarterly crowned with a princely bonnet proper; and second, or, the imperial eagle of Russia, charged on the breast with a shield of Muscovy encircled by the collar of the Order of Saint Andrew the First-Called, and on the wings with those of the tsardoms of Kazan, Astrakhan, Poland, Siberia and Tauride, of the Kingdom of Georgia, of the Grand Duchies of Kiev, Vladimir and Novgorod and of Finland
blasons.D'azur à une flèche et une ancre d'argen: Azure, an arrow and an anchor argent in saltire beneath a star or, all within a bordure argent charged with eight roses gules barbed or (alternative arms, 1858); two anchors in saltire behind the shield
blasons.D'azur à deux haches d'or passées en sau: Azure, two axes or in saltire within a wreath of roses argent seeded gules, the whole with a bordure sable charged with eight lion's heads alternately or and argent (alternative arms, 1858); two axes in saltire behind the shield
blasons.D'argent au griffon de gueules tenant un: Argent, a griffin gules holding a sword of the same and a round shield or, a bend gules, all within a bordure sable with eight lions' heads alternately or and argent (alternative arms, 1858); two cannons in saltire behind the shield
blasons.D'azur, à la croix alésée d'argent (de G: Azure, a cross couped argent (Greece), overall, quarterly, simplified Glücksburg: a cross formy argent fimbriated gules, which is the Dannebrog, between in I, or, nine hearts gules, in three pales, three lions passant azure, armed and langued gules, crowned of the field, over all (Denmark); in II, or, two lions passant azure, armed and langued gules (Schleswig); in III, gules, a nettle leaf argent (Holstein), in IV gules, a horse's head couped or (Lauenburg); over all of all, per pale or, two bars gules (Oldenburg) and azure, a cross formy fitched or (Delmenhorst). Simple version: Azure, a cross couped argent (Greece)

Azure, a cross couped argent (Greece); overall, quarterly, by a cross pattée argent fimbriated gules, the Dannebrog, with in I, or, nine hearts gules in three pales, three lions passant azure, armed and langued gules, crowned of the field, overall (Denmark); in II, or, two lions passant azure, armed and langued gules (Schleswig); in III, per fess: A, azure, three crowns or (Sweden Modern), and B, per fess gules, a cod skin argent held in pale by a crossbar sable, the whole crowned or, and azure, a ram passant argent langued gules and armed or, and azure, a polar bear argent armed of the first; in IV, per fess or, a lion passant azure above nine hearts gules set 5 and 4 (Kingdom of the Goths) and gules, a dragon or (Kingdom of the Vandals); overall, quarterly: 1, gules, a nettle leaf argent (Holstein); 2, gules, a swan argent, beaked, membered and gorged with a crown or (Stormarn); 3, gules, a horseman armed argent (Dithmarschen); 4, gules, a horse's head couped or (Lauenburg); over all of that, per pale or, two fesses gules (Oldenburg) and azure, a cross pattée with a fitched foot or (Delmenhorst)
blasons.Parti en I, écartelé au 1 de gueules au: Per pale: I, quarterly, 1, gules, a castle or, roofed and masoned azure (Castile), 2, argent, a lion gules armed, langued and crowned or (León), 3, or, four pallets gules (Aragon), 4, gules, chains or set in orle, cross and saltire, charged at the centre with an emerald proper (Navarre), accompanied in base by argent, a pomegranate gules stalked and leaved vert (Granada), and overall azure, three fleurs-de-lis or, a bordure gules (Anjou); II, azure, a cross couped argent (Greece); overall, quarterly, by a cross pattée argent fimbriated gules, the Dannebrog, with in I, or, nine hearts gules in three pales, three lions passant azure, armed and langued gules, crowned of the field, overall (Denmark); in II, or, two lions passant azure, armed and langued gules (Schleswig); in III, per fess: A, azure, three crowns or (Sweden Modern), and B, per fess gules, a cod skin argent held in pale by a crossbar sable, the whole crowned or, and azure, a ram passant argent langued gules and armed or, and azure, a polar bear argent armed of the first; in IV, per fess or, a lion passant azure above nine hearts gules set 5 and 4 (Kingdom of the Goths) and gules, a dragon or (Kingdom of the Vandals); overall, quarterly: 1, gules, a nettle leaf argent (Holstein); 2, gules, a swan argent, beaked, membered and gorged with a crown or (Stormarn); 3, gules, a horseman armed argent (Dithmarschen); 4, gules, a horse's head couped or (Lauenburg); over all of that, per pale or, two fesses gules (Oldenburg) and azure, a cross pattée with a fitched foot or (Delmenhorst)
blasons.Parti : au I écartelé, au 1 et 4 de gueu: Per pale: I, quarterly, 1 and 4, gules, three lions passant guardant or armed and langued azure (England); 2, or, a lion gules within a double tressure flory-counter-flory of the same (Scotland); 3, azure, a harp or, stringed argent (Ireland); II, quarterly, by a cross pattée argent fimbriated gules, the Dannebrog, with in I, or, nine hearts gules in three pales, three lions passant azure, armed and langued gules, crowned of the field, overall (Denmark); in II, or, two lions passant azure, armed and langued gules (Schleswig); in III, per fess: A, azure, three crowns or (Sweden Modern), and B, per fess gules, a cod skin argent held in pale by a crossbar sable, the whole crowned or, and azure, a ram passant argent langued gules and armed or, and azure, a polar bear argent armed of the first; in IV, per fess or, a lion passant azure above nine hearts gules set 5 and 4 (Kingdom of the Goths) and gules, a dragon or (Kingdom of the Vandals); overall, quarterly: 1, gules, a nettle leaf argent (Holstein); 2, gules, a swan argent, beaked, membered and gorged with a crown or (Stormarn); 3, gules, a horseman armed argent (Dithmarschen); 4, gules, a horse's head couped or (Lauenburg); over all of that, per pale or, two fesses gules (Oldenburg) and azure, a cross pattée with a fitched foot or (Delmenhorst)
blasons.Ecartelé, au I d'or, à neuf cœurs de gue: Quarterly: I, or, nine hearts gules in three pales, three lions passant azure, armed and langued gules, crowned of the field (Denmark); II, azure, a cross argent (Greece); III, argent, two pallets sable (Mountbatten (Battenberg)); IV, argent, a castle triple-towered, masoned argent and open gules, on a mount (Edinburgh)
blasons.Ecartelé : à la croix pattée d'argent bo: Quarterly: a cross formy argent fimbriated gules, which is the Dannebrog, between in I, or, nine hearts gules, in three pales, three lions passant azure, armed and langued gules, crowned of the field, over all (Denmark); in II, gules, a crowned lion or, holding in its paws a Danish axe argent, hafted of the second (ancient Norway); in III, azure, three crowns or (modern Sweden); in IV, or, a lion passant azure above nine hearts gules arranged 5 and 4 (Kingdom of the Goths); in the base, gules, a dragon or (Kingdom of the Vandals); overall, quarterly: 1, or, two lions passant azure, armed and langued gules (Schleswig); 2, gules, a nettle leaf argent (Holstein); 3, gules, a swan argent, beaked, membered and gorged with a crown or (Stormarn); 4, gules, an armed horseman argent (Dithmarschen); over all of all, per pale or, two bars gules (Oldenburg) and azure, a cross formy fitched or (Delmenhorst); a label argent, each point charged with three ermine spots sable, over the division
blasons.Ecartelé : aux I et IV contre-écartelé d: Quarterly: I and IV, quarterly azure, three fleurs-de-lis or, and gules, three lions passant guardant or; II, or, a lion gules, within a double tressure flory counter-flory of the same; azure, a harp or, stringed argent; overall or, nine hearts gules, in three pales, three lions passant azure, armed and langued gules, crowned of the field, over all (Denmark); a label argent over the division, the second point charged with a Cross of Saint George gules
blasons.De gueules, au lion couronné d'or, tenan: Gules, a crowned lion or, holding in its paws an axe argent, hafted of the second
blasons.D'or, au lion de sable, armé et lampassé: Or, a lion sable, armed and langued gules
blasons.Écartelé : aux I et IV, d'azur au lion b: Quarterly: I and IV, azure, a lion barry argent and gules (Thuringia); II and III, or, a lion sable (Meissen)
blasons.Burelé de sable et d'or, au crancelin de: Barry sable and or, a crancelin vert in bend overall (Saxony). Arch-Marshalship of the Holy Roman Empire, an office attached to the electorate: per fess sable and argent, two swords gules in saltire
Barry sable and or, a crancelin vert in bend overall (Saxony). Arch-Marshalship of the Holy Roman Empire: per fess sable and argent, two swords gules in saltire
blasons.Écartelé : en I, burelé de dix pièces de: Quarterly: I, barry of ten sable and or, a crancelin vert (Saxony); II, azure, a lion barry argent and gules, crowned or (Thuringia); III, azure, an eagle or (Palatinate of Saxony); IV, or, a lion sable, armed and langued gules (Meissen)
blasons.Parti de deux, coupé de trois : I, d'azu: Per pale of two, per fess of three: I, azure, an eagle or (Palatinate of Saxony); II, azure, a lion barry argent and gules, crowned or (Thuringia); III, or, a lion sable (Meissen); IV, or, semé of hearts gules, a lion sable (Orlamünde); V, in surtout, barry sable and or, a crancelin vert (Saxony); VI, azure, a lion per fess or and argent (Pleissen); VII, argent, three chapes gules (Engern); VIII, or, two pallets azure (Landsberg); IX, sable, an eagle or (Palatinate of Thuringia); X, gules (right of regalia); the page gives other quarters
blasons.Parti de deux et coupé de cinq : I, d'az: Per pale of two and per fess of five: I, azure, a lion barry argent and gules, crowned or (Thuringia); II, gules, an escutcheon argent, an escarbuncle or (Cleves); III, or, a lion sable (Meissen); IV, or, a lion sable (Jülich); V, in surtout, barry sable and or, a crancelin vert (Saxony); VI, argent, a lion gules, armed and langued azure, crowned or (Berg); VII, azure, an eagle or (Palatinate of Saxony); VIII, or, two pallets azure (Landsberg); IX, sable, an eagle or (Palatinate of Thuringia); the page gives other quarters
blasons.Armes moyennes : écartelé : I, d'azur au: Middle arms: quarterly: I, azure, a lion barry argent and gules, crowned or (Thuringia); II, or, a lion sable, armed and langued gules (Meissen); III, or, a hen sable, crested, beaked and membered gules, on a mount vert; IV, sable, a lion or, armed, langued and crowned gules (Vogtland); overall, barry sable and or, a crancelin vert in bend overall (Saxony)
blasons.Écartelé : I et IV, contre-écartelé : au: Quarterly: I and IV, quarterly: 1 and 4, gules, three lions passant guardant or, armed and langued azure (England); 2, or, a lion gules within a double tressure flory counter-flory of the same (Scotland); 3, azure, a harp or stringed argent (Ireland), a label of three points argent, the centre one charged with a cross gules (of Saint George); II and III, barruly of ten sable and or, a crancelin vert bendwise over all (Saxony)

blasons.De sinople, à la sphère armillaire d'or: Vert, an armillary sphere or on a cross of the Order of Christ, surrounded by a ring azure charged with twenty stars argent; overall, an escutcheon barry sable and or, a crancelin vert
blasons.Écartelé : en I, burelé de dix pièces de: Quarterly: I, barry of ten sable and or, a crancelin vert; II, azure, a lion barry argent and gules, crowned or (Thuringia); III, dimidiated: 1, gules, an eagle argent, beaked, langued, membered, jessed and crowned or (Poland), 2, barry of eight gules and argent (Hungary); IV, or, two pallets azure (Landsberg); overall, per fess sable and argent, two swords gules in saltire (Arch-Marshalship)

blasons.D'or à l'aigle de sable, membrée, becqué: Or, an eagle sable, membered, beaked and jessed gules; overall, quarterly: 1 and 4, sable, a lion or, armed, langued and crowned gules; 2 and 3, bendy-lozengy azure and argent

blasons.Écartelé : aux 1 et 4, fuselé en bande d: Quarterly: 1 and 4, bendy-lozengy azure and argent; 2 and 3, sable, a lion or, armed, langued and crowned gules; overall, gules, an orb crossed or
blasons.D'or à l'aigle de sable, membrée, becqué: Or, an eagle sable, membered, beaked and jessed gules; overall, bendy-lozengy azure and argent

blasons.Parti : fuselé en bande d'azur et d'arge: Per pale: bendy-lozengy azure and argent; and argent, an eagle gules, armed, beaked and langued or
blasons.Écartelé : aux 1 et 4, fuselé en bande d: Quarterly: 1 and 4, bendy-lozengy azure and argent; 2 and 3, quarterly: 1 and 4, or, a lion sable, armed and langued gules, 2 and 3, or, a lion gules, armed and langued azure
blasons.Parti : en I, écartelé : aux 1 et 4, de: Per pale: I, quarterly: 1 and 4, sable, a lion or, armed, langued and crowned gules (Palatinate of the Rhine); 2 and 3, bendy-lozengy azure and argent (Bavaria); overall, argent, a lion azure, armed, langued and crowned or (Veldenz); II, per fess of two, per pale of three: or, a lion sable (Jülich); gules, an escutcheon argent, an escarbuncle or (Cleves); argent, a lion gules with forked tail, crowned or (Berg); or, a fess chequy argent and gules of three tracts (La Marck); the page gives other quarters
blasons.Écartelé : à la croix pattée d'or (croix: Quarterly, by a cross pattée or (cross of Saint Eric), with 1 and 4, Sweden Modern (azure, three crowns or, set 2 and 1), 2 and 3, Sweden Ancient (azure, three bends sinister wavy argent, overall a lion crowned or); overall, quarterly: 1, bendy-lozengy azure and argent (Bavaria); 2, or, a lion sable (Jülich); 3, gules, an escutcheon argent, an escarbuncle or (Cleves); 4, argent, a lion gules with forked tail, crowned or (Berg); the page gives other quarters
blasons.Palatinat en Bavière, 1799-1804 : parti: Palatinate in Bavaria, 1799-1804: per pale; 1, or, a lion sable with forked tail in saltire, crowned or (Jülich); 2, argent, a lion gules with forked tail in saltire, crowned azure (Berg); 3, gules, an escutcheon argent, an escarbuncle or (Cleves); 4, or, a fess sable (Sponheim); 5, chequy argent and gules of three tracts (Birkenfeld); the page gives other quarters
blasons.Fuselé en bande d'azur et d'argent, char: Bendy-lozengy azure and argent, charged at the centre with an escutcheon gules, a sword argent hilted or in saltire with a sceptre or, the whole surmounted by a royal crown of the same
blasons.Écartelé : au 1, de sable au lion d'or,: Quarterly: 1, sable, a lion or, armed, langued and crowned gules (Palatinate of the Rhine); 2, per fess indented of three pieces gules and argent (Franconia); 3, bendy argent and gules, overall a pale or (Burgau); 4, argent, a lion azure, armed, langued and crowned or (Veldenz); overall, bendy-lozengy azure and argent (Bavaria)
blasons.D'azur à la croix alésée d'argent, sur-l: Azure, a cross couped argent, overall fusily in bend azure and argent
blasons.D'or à la bande de gueules chargée de tr: Or, a bend gules charged with three alerions argent (Lorraine)
Or, on a bend gules three alerions argent, differenced by a label azure
Or, on a bend gules three alerions argent (Lorraine), without the label
blasons.Écartelé : aux 1 et 4, d'or à la bande d: Quarterly: 1 and 4, or, a bend gules charged with three alerions argent (Lorraine); 2 and 3, per fess: the chief tierced in pale of barry of eight gules and argent (Hungary), azure semé of fleurs-de-lis or, a label gules (Anjou-Sicily), argent, a cross potent or between four small crosses of the same (Jerusalem); in base, per pale azure semé of fleurs-de-lis or, a bordure gules (Anjou) and azure semé of crosses crosslet fitched or, two barbels addorsed of the same (Bar)
blasons.Coupé, le chef parti de trois traits : e: Per fess, the chief per pale of three lines: 1, barry of eight gules and argent (Hungary); 2, azure, semé of fleurs-de-lis or, a label gules (Anjou-Sicily); 3, argent, a cross potent or between four crosslets of the same (Jerusalem); 4, or, four pallets gules (Aragon); the base per pale azure, semé of fleurs-de-lis or, a bordure gules (Anjou) and azure, semé of crosses crosslet fitchy or, two barbel addorsed of the same (Bar); overall, or, on a bend gules three alerions argent (Lorraine)
blasons.Coupé d'un trait et parti de trois : en: Per fess of one line and per pale of three: 1, barry of eight gules and argent (Hungary); 2, Anjou-Sicily; 3, Jerusalem; 4, or, four pallets gules (Aragon); 5, Anjou; 6, azure, a lion contourné with forked tail or, armed, langued and crowned gules (Guelders); 7, or, a lion sable, armed and langued gules (Jülich); the page gives the rest and, overall, Lorraine

blasons.D'or au lion de sable, armé et lampassé: Or, a lion sable, armed and langued gules (Flanders)
blasons.Coupé et parti de trois : au premier, fa: Per fess and per pale of three: first, barry gules and argent (Hungary); second, azure, semé of lilies or, a label gules (Anjou-Sicily); third, argent, a cross potent or between four crosslets of the same (Jerusalem); fourth, or, four pallets gules (Aragon); fifth, per pale azure, semé of lilies or, a bordure gules (Anjou); sixth, azure, a lion contourné or (Guelders); seventh, or, a lion sable (Jülich); eighth, azure, semé of crosslets or, two barbel or (Bar); overall, or, on a bend gules three alerions argent, the whole differenced by a label gules
blasons.Mi-parti de France (d'azur à trois fleur: Dimidiated France (azure, three fleurs-de-lis or) and Lorraine (per fess and per pale of three: Hungary, Anjou-Sicily with a label gules, Jerusalem, Aragon, Anjou, Guelders, Jülich, Bar; overall, or, a bend gules charged with three alerions argent)

textes.Après la mort de Marie, Guillaume III ga: After Mary's death, William III kept his own arms alone.
textes.François devient roi de France en 1559 :: Francis became King of France in 1559: Mary's arms followed her rank as queen consort.
textes.Veuve de François en 1560, Marie garde l: Widowed of Francis in 1560, Mary kept the impalement until her remarriage to Darnley in 1565, then went back to the lion alone.

textes.Ferdinand, roi de Bohême et de Hongrie: Ferdinand, King of Bohemia and Hungary

textes.François II fonde l'empire d'Autriche et: Francis II founded the Austrian Empire and took its double-headed eagle.

textes.Béatrice, reine de Castille et de Portug: Beatrice, Queen of Castile and Portugal
textes.Alphonse V réclame la couronne de Castil: Alfonso V claimed the crown of Castile from 1475 to 1479: his arms bear Portugal in the 1st and 4th quarters, Castile and León in the 2nd and 3rd.
textes.Prêtre, Henri fait ajouter à la couronne: A priest, Henry had the red hat and tassels of his rank as cardinal added to the royal crown: a composition unique to his reign.
textes.Charles-Albert, de la branche de Carigna: Charles Albert, of the Carignano branch, took up the arms of 1720, adding Genoa, Nice, Piedmont and Saluzzo, but in practice preferred the small shield with the cross alone.
textes.Nassau (comtes de Laurenbourg puis de Na: Nassau (Counts of Laurenburg, then of Nassau)
textes.Blasonnement de la ligne des premiers co: Blazon of the line of the first counts (Dudo of Laurenburg and successors) as the armorial gives it; the Commons page cites Rietstap.
textes.Blasonnement attribué par l'armorial à V: Blazon attributed by the armorial to Walram II (co-Count of Nassau from 1249 to 1255).
textes.L'armorial donne ce même blasonnement po: The armorial gives this same blazon for Otto II (died 1350) and for William the Rich (1487-1559): see the disagreement on the incoming link.
textes.La fiche Commons précise que ces armes n: The Commons page specifies that these arms do not reproduce a period appearance but are reconstructed from descriptions and historical sources.
textes.Blasonnement d'Ernest-Casimir de Nassau-: Blazon of Ernest Casimir of Nassau-Dietz according to the armorial; I have not checked that the Commons image reproduces this blazon exactly.
textes.Blasonnement de Jean-Guillaume-Friso sel: Blazon of John William Friso according to the armorial; not checked that the image reproduces every detail.

textes.Charles XIII, roi de Suède et de Norvège: Charles XIII, King of Sweden and Norway

textes.La page lue donne ces armes à Boris III: The page read gives these arms to Boris III (King of the Bulgarians, 1918-1943) and to Simeon II (king, 1943-1946, then Prime Minister of the Republic of Bulgaria from 2001 to 2005 as Simeon Sakskoburggotski).
textes.Jean-Georges Ier, électeur de Saxe: John George I, Elector of Saxony
textes.Frédéric-Auguste le Juste, roi de Saxe: Frederick Augustus the Just, King of Saxony
textes.La page lue donne aussi des grandes arme: The page read also gives great arms of the kingdom (Meissen, Thuringia, the two Palatinates, Vogtland and other quarters); only the lesser arms are shown here.
textes.Othon Ier reçoit en 1180 de Frédéric Bar: Otto I received from Frederick Barbarossa in 1180 the Duchy of Bavaria, confiscated from Henry the Lion; the page gives this fusily for the Dukes of Bavaria from 1180 to 1623.
textes.Frédéric V, électeur palatin et roi de B: Frederick V, Elector Palatine and King of Bohemia
textes.Rois de Suède de la maison palatine: Kings of Sweden of the Palatine house
textes.Maximilien, de Deux-Ponts à la couronne: Maximilian, from Zweibrücken to the crown of Bavaria
textes.Glasshouse, d'après des éléments de Soda: Glasshouse, after elements by Sodacan and Heralder
textes.Ducs de Lorraine, de Simon II à Charles: Dukes of Lorraine, from Simon II to Charles II
textes.Il s'agissait à l'origine de trois aigle: Originally these were three eaglets whose legs and beak atrophied to become the present alerion, at the end of the 15th century (page read).
textes.Antoine de Vaudémont, chef de la maison: Anthony of Vaudémont, head of the house
textes.La figure est la même que celle des ducs: The figure is the same as that of the earlier Dukes of Lorraine: the label azure has been removed.
textes.René II, armes de ses deux parents: René II, arms of both his parents
textes.Ducs de Lorraine, de René II à Antoine (: Dukes of Lorraine, from René II to Anthony (c. 1538)
textes.Ducs de Lorraine, d'Antoine (vers 1538): Dukes of Lorraine, from Anthony (c. 1538) to Francis III (1737)
textes.La page renvoie à la partie Habsbourg-Lo: The page refers to the Habsburg-Lorraine part of the Armorial of the Habsburgs for his descendants.
textes.À partir de la seconde moitié du XIVe si: From the second half of the 14th century, a shield gyronny or and azure with an escutcheon gules overall (Flanders Ancient) was attributed retrospectively to the predecessors of Philip of Alsace.
textes.Louise de Lorraine, reine de France: Louise of Lorraine, Queen of France
textes.Le blasonnement est résumé : la page don: The blazon is summarised: the page gives the detail of the eight Lorraine quarters.
textes.Bourbon, rois de France et de Navarre: Bourbon, kings of France and Navarre

textes.Christian X, roi d'Islande aussi: Christian X, also King of Iceland
textes.Henri de Monpezat, époux de la reine: Henrik de Monpezat, the Queen's husband
textes.Georges II, roi des Hellènes: George II, King of the Hellenes
textes.Sofía de Grèce, reine d'Espagne: Sofía of Greece, Queen of Spain
textes.Jean-Frédéric, déposé de l'électorat: John Frederick, deprived of the electorate
textes.Prétendants au trône du Brésil: Claimants to the throne of Brazil
textes.René II : les armes de ses deux parents: René II: the arms of both his parents
textes.Brisure : d'abord une bordure-lambel de: Difference: first a bordure-label gules, then (after 1297) a bordure gules on the semé of lilies.
textes.Charles de Valois est le frère cadet du: Charles of Valois is the younger brother of King Philip the Fair: he keeps the King's lilies, differenced by a mark distinguishing him from the elder.
textes.La brisure disparaît : avec Philippe VI,: The difference disappears: with Philip VI, the royal shield goes back to the semé of France alone.
textes.Louis X, Philippe V puis Charles IV meur: Louis X, Philip V and then Charles IV died without a surviving son. Daughters were set aside under the custom fixed ten years earlier, and Edward III of England, grandson of Philip the Fair through his mother, was ousted: the peers refused to give the crown to a foreign king. Philip of Valois, son of Charles of Valois, descended from the Capetians through the male line: he was chosen and crowned on 29 May 1328.
textes.Brisure : un lambel d'argent sur les tro: Difference: a label argent on the three lilies.
textes.Louis, duc d'Orléans, est le frère de Ch: Louis, Duke of Orléans, is the brother of Charles VI: he keeps the King's arms, differenced by a label argent.
textes.Le lambel d'Orléans reçoit trois pendant: The label of Orléans receives three points, each charged with a crescent gules.
textes.Jean d'Orléans, comte d'Angoulême, est l: John of Orléans, Count of Angoulême, is the third son of Louis of Orléans: he keeps his father's label argent and distinguishes it with the crescents.
textes.Au lambel d'argent s'ajoute une barre d': To the label argent is added a bend sinister argent overall.
textes.Jean d'Orléans, comte de Dunois, est le: John of Orléans, Count of Dunois, is the illegitimate son of Louis of Orléans: he bears his father's arms, but with a bend sinister.
textes.Écartelé de Bade-Hochberg et de Neuchâte: Quarterly Baden-Hochberg and Neuchâtel, with overall the arms of Orléans-Longueville, label and baton couped in bend.
textes.François d'Orléans-Rothelin est le fils: Francis of Orléans-Rothelin is the illegitimate son of Francis II of Orléans-Longueville: he keeps his father's arms, with a baton couped in bend.
textes.La page lue ne dit pas pourquoi les quar: The page read does not say why the quarters of Baden-Hochberg and Neuchâtel surround the shield.
textes.Brisure : une bordure de gueules sur le: Difference: a bordure gules on the semé of lilies.
textes.La page lue ne dit pas pourquoi la bordu: The page read does not say why the bordure is gules.
textes.Louis, deuxième fils du roi Jean le Bon,: Louis, second son of King John the Good, received from his father as an appanage the Duchy of Anjou and the County of Maine in 1360; the armorial gives him the difference of a bordure gules.
textes.Brisure : une bordure de gueules chargée: Difference: a bordure gules charged with bezants argent on the semé of lilies.
textes.Charles II, comte d'Alençon, est le fils: Charles II, Count of Alençon, is the son of Charles of Valois: he keeps his father's semé of lilies and charges the bordure with bezants argent.
textes.Brisure : une bordure componée d'argent: Difference: a bordure compony argent and gules on the semé of lilies.
textes.Philippe le Hardi est le fils de Jean II: Philip the Bold is the son of John II, King of France: he keeps the semé of lilies, differenced by a bordure compony.
textes.Écartelé : aux 1 et 4 les lis à la bordu: Quarterly: 1 and 4, the lilies with the bordure compony of Valois-Burgundy; 2, a lion or on sable; 3, a lion gules on argent.
textes.La page lue ne dit pas à quel titre il s: The page read does not say in what capacity he succeeded Joanna, or where the two lions come from.
textes.Antoine, de la maison de Valois-Bourgogn: Anthony, of the House of Valois-Burgundy, succeeded Joanna of Brabant as Duke of Brabant and Limburg in 1406; he died at Agincourt in 1415.
textes.Écartelé : aux 1 et 4 les lis à la bordu: Quarterly: 1 and 4, the lilies with the bordure compony; 2 and 3, a lion sable on or.
textes.Philippe, comte de Nevers et de Rethel,: Philip, Count of Nevers and Rethel, is the son of Philip the Bold: he keeps his father's arms.
textes.La page ne dit pas d'où vient le lion de: The page does not say where the lion sable of quarters 2 and 3 comes from.
textes.Brisure : un lambel de gueules dont chaq: Difference: a label gules with each point bearing three castles or.
textes.Robert est le troisième fils de Louis VI: Robert is the third son of Louis VIII and Blanche of Castile. Like his brothers Alphonse of Poitiers and Charles of Anjou, he puts in his difference the castles from his mother's arms; his descendants in the male line keep them.
textes.Brisure : un lambel de gueules sur le se: Difference: a label gules on the semé of lilies.
textes.Charles d'Anjou est un frère de Robert d: Charles of Anjou is a brother of Robert of Artois, son of Louis VIII: he keeps the King's lilies, differenced by a label gules.
textes.Brisure : une bande componée d'argent et: Difference: a bend compony argent and gules on the semé of lilies.
textes.Louis, comte d'Évreux, est le fils de Ph: Louis, Count of Évreux, is the son of Philip III: he keeps the King's lilies, differenced by a bend compony.
textes.Les lis sont abandonnés : le champ est d: The lilies are given up: the field is or, three roundels gules.
textes.Pierre, fils de Louis VI, épouse Élisabe: Peter, son of Louis VI, married Elizabeth of Courtenay, whose name and arms he took.
textes.Armes propres : échiqueté d'or et d'azur: Arms of their own: chequy or and azure, without the lilies.
textes.L'armorial nomme Raoul Ier comme premier: The armorial names Ralph I as the first bearer; the page read on Hugh, very brief, gives neither the date of his marriage nor the passage from Hugh to Ralph.
textes.Hugues de Vermandois (1057-1102), fils d: Hugh of Vermandois (1057-1102), son of King Henry I, married the heiress of the County of Vermandois: the branch took the name of that county.
textes.Échiqueté d'or et d'azur, à la bordure d: Chequy or and azure, a bordure gules.
textes.Robert, comte de Dreux, est le fils de L: Robert, Count of Dreux, is the son of Louis VI.
textes.Le même échiqueté d'or et d'azur est por: The same chequy or and azure is borne, on the same page, by the House of Vermandois; the page does not say why Dreux takes it.
textes.Brisure : la bordure de gueules devient: Difference: the bordure gules becomes engrailed.
textes.Robert de Dreux, seigneur de Beu, est le: Robert of Dreux, Lord of Beu, is the son of Robert III, Count of Dreux: he keeps his father's chequy and changes its bordure.
textes.Un franc-quartier d'hermine s'ajoute à l: A quarter ermine is added to the chequy with the bordure gules.
textes.La page lue ne dit pas comment l'hermine: The page read does not say how the ermine of Brittany entered his shield.
textes.Pierre de Dreux, d'ascendance capétienne: Peter of Dreux, of Capetian descent, was betrothed to Alix of Thouars, Duchess of Brittany: he paid liege homage for Brittany to Philip Augustus in 1213 and governed the duchy as bailiff from 1213 to 1237; the marriage took place only a little later.
textes.Armes toutes autres : d'argent à trois c: Entirely different arms: argent, three chevrons gules.
textes.Olivier de Machecoul est le fils de Pier: Oliver of Machecoul is the son of Peter Mauclerc.
textes.La page ne dit pas pourquoi il ne porte: The page does not say why he bears neither the chequy nor the ermine of his father.
textes.Écartelé d'hermine, avec des quartiers c: Quarterly ermine, with counter-quartered quarters: the lilies with a label argent and a serpent (guivre) azure.
textes.François d'Avaugour est le fils de Franç: Francis of Avaugour is the son of Francis II of Brittany.
textes.La page ne dit pas d'où viennent le lamb: The page does not say where the label and serpent of the quarters come from.
textes.Armes propres : bandé d'or et d'azur de: Arms of their own: bendy of six or and azure, a bordure gules — not the lilies.
textes.Robert, fils du roi Robert II le Pieux,: Robert, son of King Robert II the Pious, became Duke of Burgundy in 1032 and founded the first Capetian house of the duchy. Odo II is the first to bear these arms (1143).
textes.Pourquoi le duché porte ses propres arme: Why the duchy bears arms of its own and not the King's lilies: the sources read do not say.
textes.Armes propres : d'argent, croix d'azur (: Arms of their own: argent, a cross azure (according to the page read).
textes.La page lue ne dit pas pourquoi les arme: The page read does not say why the arms of Portugal are entirely different from those of Burgundy.
textes.Henri de Bourgogne épouse Thérèse de Leó: Henry of Burgundy married Theresa of León in 1093 and received from Alfonso VI of León the lands south of the Minho, the origin of the County of Portugal.
textes.Brisure : une bande de gueules sur le se: Difference: a bend gules on the semé of lilies.
textes.Robert, comte de Clermont, est un fils d: Robert, Count of Clermont, is a son of Saint Louis: he keeps the King's lilies, differenced by a bend gules.
textes.Les trois lis, avec une bande engrêlée d: The three lilies, with a bend engrailed gules.
textes.Louis, comte de Montpensier et dauphin d: Louis, Count of Montpensier and Dauphin of Auvergne, is the son of John I of Bourbon: he keeps the arms of Bourbon and engrails the bend.
textes.Brisure : trois lionceaux d'argent sur l: Difference: three lioncels argent on the bend gules.
textes.Jacques, comte de la Marche, est le fils: James, Count of La Marche, is the son of Louis I of Bourbon: he keeps the bend of Bourbon and charges it with lioncels.
textes.Écartelé : aux 1 et 4 Bourbon-La Marche,: Quarterly: 1 and 4, Bourbon-La Marche; 2 and 3, an eagle or on gules.
textes.Jacques, seigneur de Préaux, est le fils: James, Lord of Préaux, is the son of James I of La Marche.
textes.La page ne dit pas d'où vient l'aigle d': The page does not say where the eagle or of quarters 2 and 3 comes from.
textes.Le champ est d'argent : une bande d'azur: The field is argent: a bend azure semé of lilies, with a cotise gules.
textes.La page lue ne dit pas pourquoi les émau: The page read does not say why the tinctures are reversed (field argent, bend azure).
textes.Charles de Bourbon-Lavedan, dit « bâtard: Charles of Bourbon-Lavedan, known as “the bastard of Bourbon”, illegitimate son of John II of Bourbon and Joan Louise of Albret, is the origin of the illegitimate branch of Bourbon-Lavedan.
textes.Écartelé : aux 1 et 4 les lis ; aux 2 et: Quarterly: 1 and 4, the lilies; 2 and 3, a lion azure on argent with a chief gules; overall, the bend of Bourbon-La Marche.
textes.Louis, comte de Vendôme, est le fils de: Louis, Count of Vendôme, is the son of John I of La Marche: he keeps the arms of Bourbon and places in them the lion of Vendôme.
textes.La page nomme Louis « comte de Vendôme »: The page calls Louis “Count of Vendôme” but does not explicitly link the lion azure to this county.
textes.Les trois lis, avec un bâton de gueules: The three lilies, with a baton gules charged with a crescent argent, and a quarter.
textes.Louis, prince de La Roche-sur-Yon, est l: Louis, Prince of La Roche-sur-Yon, is the son of John VIII of Vendôme: he keeps the lilies and differences them with a baton.
textes.Écartelé : aux 1 et 4 les trois lis au b: Quarterly: 1 and 4, the three lilies with a baton gules couped in bend; 2 and 3, a lion gules with forked tail in saltire.
textes.François, comte de Saint-Pol, est le fil: Francis, Count of Saint-Pol, is the son of Francis of Vendôme and Mary of Luxembourg.
textes.La page nomme sa mère Marie de Luxembour: The page names his mother Mary of Luxembourg; it does not say that the lion with forked tail of quarters 2 and 3 comes from this house.
textes.Les trois lis, avec une bande de gueules: The three lilies, with a bend gules charged in the quarter with a bezant argent.
textes.Louis, prince de Condé, est le fils de C: Louis, Prince of Condé, is the son of Charles IV, Duke of Vendôme: he keeps the arms of his house, differenced by a bezant.
textes.Semé de France à la cotice de gueules en: Semé of France with a cotise gules in bend, on a chief argent a cross potent or (Jerusalem).
textes.Pierre de Bourbon, baron de Busset, est: Peter of Bourbon, Baron of Busset, is the natural son of Louis of Bourbon, Prince-Bishop of Liège: he bears the arms of France, with a cotise.
textes.La page ne dit pas pourquoi la croix de: The page does not say why the cross of Jerusalem decorates the chief.
textes.Les trois lis sont partis avec les chaîn: The three lilies are impaled with the chains of Navarre.
textes.Henri de Bourbon est le fils d'Antoine d: Henry of Bourbon is the son of Anthony of Bourbon, Duke of Vendôme, and Joan of Albret, and a descendant of Saint Louis in the male line. He had been King of Navarre since 1572, on his mother's death. When the younger brother of Henry III, Francis of Anjou, died without an heir in 1584, the childless King considered confirming him as lawful heir; assassinated on 1 August 1589, Henry III in turn recognised him as his successor. Henry IV then bore the lilies and the chains of Navarre impaled.
textes.Les armes d'Espagne portent en cœur l'éc: The arms of Spain bear at the centre the escutcheon of Anjou (three lilies, at first with a bordure gules).
Charles II of Spain died childless. Genealogy pointed to the Grand Dauphin, son of Maria Theresa, elder sister of the late King and wife of Louis XIV; Austria defended the rights of Archduke Charles. To avoid the dismemberment of his States, Charles II chose Philip, Duke of Anjou, second grandson of Louis XIV: he judged the King of France the most capable of defending the inheritance. Louis XIV accepted the will on 16 November 1700; Emperor Leopold disputed it.
textes.Les trois lis à la bordure de gueules, s: The three lilies with a bordure gules, without the Spanish quarters.
textes.Jacques-Henri, deuxième fils d'Alphonse: James Henry, second son of Alfonso XIII, was titled Duke of Anjou and Segovia: he bears the arms of Anjou.
textes.Écartelé de Castille, de León, d'Aragon: Quarterly Castile, León, Aragon and Navarre, with Granada in base and, overall, the lilies with a bordure gules.
textes.Juan, comte de Barcelone, est le troisiè: Juan, Count of Barcelona, is the third son of Alfonso XIII and claimant to the Spanish throne from 1941 to 1977: he bears the quarters of the kingdom.
textes.Parti de trois : Farnèse et Portugal, Ca: Per pale of three: Farnese and Portugal, Castile-León and Naples, Tuscany; overall, Anjou.
textes.La page lue ne détaille pas l'entrée des: The page read does not detail how the quarters of Portugal and Tuscany entered the arms.
textes.Charles, duc de Parme et Plaisance en 17: Charles, Duke of Parma and Piacenza in 1731 on the death of his great-uncle Antonio Farnese, became King of Naples in 1734 then of Sicily in 1735, “by conquest” of these two kingdoms.
textes.Brisure : une bordure de gueules chargée: Difference: a bordure gules charged with eight escallops argent.
textes.La page lue ne dit pas d'où viennent la: The page read does not say where the bordure gules and the eight escallops come from.
textes.Le traité d'Aix-la-Chapelle, qui met fin: The Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle, ending the War of the Austrian Succession, assigned Parma, Piacenza and Guastalla to the Infante Philip, who became duke in 1748.
textes.Écartelé : aux quartiers I et IV les lis: Quarterly: I and IV, the lilies differenced by a bordure gules (Bourbon-Spain); II and III, Nassau (billety, with the lion).
textes.Jean, grand-duc de Luxembourg, est le fi: John, Grand Duke of Luxembourg, is the son of Grand Duchess Charlotte of Luxembourg and Felix of Bourbon-Parma: his father's and his mother's arms share the shield.
textes.Les trois lis au lambel d'argent : les a: The three lilies with a label argent: the arms of Orléans.
textes.Philippe de France, fils de Louis XIII,: Philip of France, son of Louis XIII, was first Duke of Anjou; he inherited the Duchy of Orléans on the death of his uncle Gaston and took up its arms.
textes.Une sphère armillaire d'or, entourée d'u: An armillary sphere or, surrounded by a ring of twenty stars, bears at the centre the shield of Orléans (three lilies with a label argent).
textes.Isabelle, fille de l'empereur Pierre II: Isabel, daughter of Emperor Peter II of Brazil, established herself as heiress to the empire. On 15 October 1864 she married Gaston of Orléans, Count of Eu, grandson of Louis Philippe: this marriage is the founding act of the Brazilian branch of Orléans, which took the name Orléans-Braganza.
textes.Les armes d'Orléans (France au lambel d': The arms of Orléans (France with a label argent) gave way to a shield bearing the Charter.
textes.Le 13 août 1830, Louis-Philippe fait gra: On 13 August 1830 Louis Philippe had the arms of his house, France with a label argent, engraved on the seal of State. After the riots of February 1831, an ordinance of 16 February replaced them with a shield bearing the Charter of 1830.
textes.Écartelé d'une aigle d'argent et d'un ch: Quarterly an eagle argent and a knight argent, with overall the three lilies of France.
textes.Henri est élu roi de Pologne le 11 mai 1: Henry was elected King of Poland on 11 May 1573 and crowned at Wawel on 21 February 1574; he reigned until 1575, then bore only the three lilies.
textes.Les armes de fils de France sont écartel: The arms of a son of France are quartered with the old arms of Burgundy.
textes.Philippe de Rouvres, dernier duc de la m: Philip of Rouvres, last duke of the Capetian house, died of plague in 1361, aged fifteen. John II, King of France, had married in 1350 his mother Joan of Boulogne, regent of the duchy: he claimed the duchy, which he gave in 1364 to his son Philip the Bold. The latter quartered his arms as a son of France with the old arms of the duchy.
textes.Les anciennes armes du duché (bandé d'or: The old arms of the duchy (bendy or and azure, a bordure gules) become quarters of the quartering.
textes.Le duché change de maison à la mort de s: The duchy changed house on the death of its last Capetian duke: its arms did not disappear, they entered the shield of the new duke.
textes.Le lion de Flandre est mis en cœur de l': The lion of Flanders is set at the centre of the shield.
textes.Le comté de Flandre était venu à la mais: The County of Flanders had come to the House of Valois-Burgundy through the marriage of Philip the Bold to Countess Margaret of Flanders. Their son John the Fearless set its lion at the centre of his shield.
textes.Le Brabant et le Limbourg entrent dans l: Brabant and Limburg enter the shield.
textes.La page parle de l'« héritage du Brabant: The page speaks of Philip the Good's “inheritance of Brabant and Limburg”: his possessions in the Netherlands grew in stages from 1427 to 1443.
textes.Les jalons de la frise parlent d'annexio: The timeline's milestones speak of annexation; the page “Philippe III de Bourgogne” speaks of inheritance.
textes.Les armes de Marie, héritière, sont port: The arms of Mary, an heiress, are borne with those of her husband Maximilian (two great parts).
textes.Charles le Téméraire meurt devant Nancy: Charles the Bold died before Nancy on 5 January 1477. His only daughter Mary, nineteen, inherited a fragile State, immediately attacked by King Louis XI.
textes.Écartelé d'Autriche, de Bourgogne modern: Quarterly Austria, Burgundy Modern, Burgundy Ancient and Brabant, with at the centre an escutcheon of Flanders and Tyrol.
textes.Marie meurt le 27 mars 1482 d'une chute: Mary died on 27 March 1482 after a fall from a horse. Her son Philip, three years old, inherited the claims to the title of Duke of Burgundy and the rest of the Burgundian State, partly occupied by the French King's army; his father Maximilian was regent. The Treaty of Arras (December 1482) ceded the Duchy and County of Burgundy to France (the county would be returned in 1493 by the Treaty of Senlis), but Mary's descendants kept the title “Duke of Burgundy”.
textes.Le Bindenschild (de gueules à la fasce d: The Bindenschild (gules, a fess argent), arms of the duchy, also becomes that of the Habsburgs.
textes.Rodolphe Ier investit ses fils du duché: Rudolf I invested his sons with the Duchy of Austria (1282): the Habsburgs took over the Bindenschild, already attested on a seal of 1230.
textes.Les armes de la Hongrie et de la Bohême,: The arms of Hungary and Bohemia, impaled, are set on the eagle of the Empire, with those of Habsburg at the centre.
textes.Albert V, duc d'Autriche, est élu roi de: Albert V, Duke of Austria, was elected King of the Romans: he placed the arms of his kingdoms on the eagle of the Empire.
textes.Les sources lues ne disent pas comment A: The sources read do not say how Albert became King of Hungary and Bohemia.
textes.L'aigle impériale à deux têtes, de sable: The double-headed imperial eagle, sable on or, replaces the single eagle.
textes.La page lue ne dit pas qu'il succède à A: The page read does not say that he succeeded Albert II.
textes.Frédéric III est élu roi des Romains en: Frederick III was elected King of the Romans in 1440 and crowned Emperor in 1452; he became Archduke of Austria in 1457 on the death of his cousin Ladislaus.
textes.L'aigle de l'Empire porte sur le tout l': The eagle of the Empire bears overall Austria impaling Burgundy.
textes.Maximilien est le fils de l'empereur Fré: Maximilian is the son of Emperor Frederick III; the Burgundian quarters are those of his marriage to Mary of Burgundy.
textes.Les quartiers bourguignons entrent dans: The Burgundian quarters enter the arms of Maximilian.
textes.Marie cherche l'appui d'un prince puissa: Mary sought the support of a powerful prince against France. She married Maximilian of Austria, son of Emperor Frederick III, by proxy on 21 April and then in person on 19 August 1477: her father had already considered this imperial alliance from 1473. Maximilian defended the Flemish provinces and Hainault; the Duchy of Burgundy and Picardy remained occupied by France.
textes.Les armes de Castille, de León, d'Aragon: The arms of Castile, León, Aragon and Granada are added to the arms of Burgundy and Austria.
textes.En 1495, Maximilien et les Rois catholiq: In 1495 Maximilian and the Catholic Monarchs concluded a pact against France providing for a double marriage of their children; Philip married Joanna of Castile on 20 October 1496. The deaths of John of Aragon (1497), Isabella (1498) and Miguel (1500) made Joanna the heiress. On the death of Isabella the Catholic (26 November 1504), Philip became king consort of Castile: his father-in-law Ferdinand disputed this, then gave way, and Philip was recognised as king in the summer of 1506. He died in September.
textes.Les quartiers d'Espagne et ceux de l'hér: The quarters of Spain and those of the Burgundian and Austrian inheritance are brought together.
textes.Philippe meurt en 1506 ; son fils Charle: Philip died in 1506; his son Charles was brought up in the Netherlands by his aunt Margaret. In 1516 he was proclaimed King of Castile and Aragon, with his mother Joanna.
textes.Les armes d'Espagne sont posées sur l'ai: The arms of Spain are set on the imperial eagle, between the Pillars of Hercules.
textes.Chef de la maison de Habsbourg en 1519,: Head of the House of Habsburg in 1519, Charles was elected Emperor in 1520; once crowned, he set his arms of Spain on the eagle.
textes.L'écu impérial passe à Charles, qui y po: The imperial shield passes to Charles, who sets on it the arms of his kingdoms.
textes.L'empire passe de Maximilien à son petit: The empire passed from Maximilian to his grandson Charles, elected in 1519-1520: he kept the eagle and changed what it bore.
textes.L'écartelé de Bohême et de Hongrie porte: The quartering of Bohemia and Hungary bears overall Austria impaling Burgundy Ancient.
textes.Après la bataille de Mohács (1526), Ferd: After the Battle of Mohács (1526), Ferdinand, married to Anne Jagiellon, “had the right to succeed to the throne of Bohemia and Hungary”; he therefore inherited through his wife.
textes.L'aigle bicéphale remplace l'écartelé de: The double-headed eagle replaces the quartering of Bohemia and Hungary.
textes.Ferdinand est élu empereur par l'assembl: Ferdinand was elected Emperor by the assembly of princes at Frankfurt on 24 March 1558; the pope's confirmation was no longer considered necessary.
textes.Un quartier de Castille écartelée de Léo: A quarter of Castile quartering León enters the shield that charges the eagle.
textes.Selon l'armorial, Maximilien II puis Jos: According to the armorial, Maximilian II then Joseph I bore the same arms as Ferdinand; the quarter of Castile appears with Rudolf II, without the sources read saying why.
textes.L'Autriche passe sur le tout du tout ; B: Austria moves over all; Burgundy Ancient is impaled with Tyrol and Flanders.
textes.La page lue ne dit pas pourquoi les arme: The page read does not say why the arms changed at this moment.
textes.Ferdinand III est élu roi des Romains le: Ferdinand III was elected King of the Romans on 22 December 1636, then became Emperor on 15 February 1637.
textes.Écartelé de Castille, de Hongrie, d'Arag: Quarterly Castile, Hungary, Aragon and Austria, with Bohemia at the centre: the arms of a King of Spain who does not reign.
textes.Charles II d'Espagne meurt sans enfant e: Charles II of Spain died childless in 1700 and chose as his heir the Duke of Anjou, grandson of Louis XIV; Austria defended the rights of Archduke Charles, who bore these arms until 1711, while disputing Spain with the grandson of Louis XIV.
textes.L'archiduc reprend à son compte les quar: The Archduke takes the quarters of Spain for himself.
textes.Voir l'autre lien : à la mort de Charles: See the other link: on the death of Charles II, without issue, Archduke Charles disputed the crown of Spain with the Duke of Anjou.
textes.L'archiduc pose sur l'aigle impériale le: The Archduke sets on the imperial eagle the arms he bore as claimant.
textes.La page lue ne développe pas ici l'ouver: The page read does not go into the opening of the succession in 1711 here.
textes.Charles VI est empereur à partir du 17 a: Charles VI was Emperor from 17 April 1711; he was elected on 12 October and crowned at Frankfurt on 22 December 1711.
textes.Les armes de Marie-Thérèse reprennent le: The arms of Maria Theresa take up the claimant to Spain, without the eagle in the armorial.
textes.Sans héritier mâle, Charles VI édicte la: Without a male heir, Charles VI issued the Pragmatic Sanction: the Habsburg domain became indivisible and women were declared able to succeed; Maria Theresa succeeded him as sovereign of Austria, Bohemia and Hungary.
textes.Les alérions de Lorraine entrent en cœur: The alerions of Lorraine enter at the centre; Tuscany appears in a quarter.
textes.Joseph II est le fils de François de Lor: Joseph II is the son of Francis of Lorraine: he is the first Habsburg-Lorraine, and his father's alerions enter at the centre of his arms.
textes.Bar et Toscane : le cœur est tiercé de L: Bar and Tuscany: the centre is tierced of Lorraine, Austria and Tuscany.
textes.L'armorial donne les armes de Léopold II: The armorial gives the arms of Leopold II and Francis II without saying why Bar enters the shield.
textes.Léopold II, frère cadet de Joseph II et: Leopold II, younger brother of Joseph II and Grand Duke of Tuscany, was elected Emperor on 30 September 1790 and crowned at Frankfurt on 9 October.
textes.Les armes de Habsbourg, d'Autriche et de: The arms of Habsburg, Austria and Lorraine (impaled) on the eagle of a hereditary empire.
textes.Les sources lues ne disent pas ce qui l': The sources read do not say what drove him to it.
textes.L'aigle bicéphale représente l'Autriche: The double-headed eagle represents Austria in the arms of the Dual Monarchy.
textes.L'empire d'Autriche et le royaume de Hon: The Austrian Empire and the Kingdom of Hungary formed the Dual Monarchy: the double-headed eagle represented Austria in its arms until 1918.
textes.Les sources lues ne disent pas pourquoi: The sources read do not say why the arms changed in 1915.
textes.Les armes d'Espagne sont accolées à cell: The arms of Spain are impaled with those of England.
textes.Philippe II porte ces armes comme monarq: Philip II bore these arms as Spanish monarch and husband of Mary I of England, from 1556 to 1558.
textes.L'écu de Portugal prend place sur le tou: The shield of Portugal takes its place over the Spanish quarters.
textes.Les pages lues ne détaillent pas la reco: The pages read do not detail the recognition of Philip II as King of Portugal.
textes.Henri Ier, le Cardinal-Roi, meurt le 31: Henry I, the Cardinal King, died on 31 January 1580; his ecclesiastical office prevented him from having legitimate issue. Philip II, son of Charles V and Isabella of Portugal, was King of Portugal from 12 September 1580.
textes.L'écusson de Portugal quitte l'écu (1668: The escutcheon of Portugal leaves the shield (1668).
textes.Le Portugal se soulève en 1640 et se don: Portugal rose up in 1640 and gave itself a king. Spain, at war with Louis XIV (War of Devolution), recognised Portuguese independence by the Treaty of Lisbon (12 February 1668) so as not to fight on two fronts.
textes.Les armes des Habsbourg d'Espagne cèdent: The arms of the Spanish Habsburgs give way to those of the Bourbons.
textes.Avec Charles II, sans descendance, s'éte: With Charles II, without issue, the Spanish branch of the House of Habsburg died out: the crown passed to the Bourbons.
textes.Castille-León et Aragon sont écartelés ;: Castile-León and Aragon are quartered; the whole on the breast of the eagle of Saint John.
textes.Isabelle de Castille et Ferdinand d'Arag: Isabella of Castile and Ferdinand of Aragon, married since 1469, united their crowns.
textes.L'Aragon et l'Aragon-Sicile occupent la: Aragon and Aragon-Sicily take up half of the quartering.
textes.Le mariage d'Isabelle et de Ferdinand d': The marriage of Isabella and Ferdinand of Aragon (1469) lies at the origin of the union of the crowns: the pallets of Aragon thus entered the shield of Castile.
textes.Un quartier de Grenade (la grenade au na: A quarter of Granada (the pomegranate proper) is enté en point.
textes.La conquête de Grenade se marque dans l': The conquest of Granada is marked in the shield by this quarter.
textes.Un écu tiercé en pal (Castille-León, Ara: A shield tierced in pale (Castile-León, Aragon-Naples-Sicily, Aragon); Navarre adds its quarter in 1513.
textes.À la mort d'Isabelle (1504), Ferdinand a: On Isabella's death (1504), Ferdinand gave up the joint arms for a shield tierced in pale; the annexation of Navarre (1513) brought the last change.
textes.Armes abrégées de Jeanne et de Charles :: Abridged arms of Joanna and Charles: Castile, León and Aragon, enté en point Granada.
textes.Les morts de Jean d'Aragon (1497), d'Isa: The deaths of John of Aragon (1497), Isabella (1498) and Miguel (1500) made Joanna, daughter of the Catholic Monarchs, the heiress; on the death of Isabella the Catholic, on 26 November 1504, the crown of Castile fell to her.
textes.Les quartiers d'Espagne entrent dans les: The quarters of Spain enter the arms of Charles.
textes.En 1516, Charles est proclamé roi de Cas: In 1516 Charles was proclaimed King of Castile and Aragon with his mother Joanna.
textes.Les quartiers espagnols des Rois catholi: The Spanish quarters of the Catholic Monarchs, with Granada, pass into the shield of Philip.
textes.C'est le mariage de 1496 avec Jeanne, fi: It was the 1496 marriage to Joanna, daughter of the Catholic Monarchs, that opened these quarters to Philip (see the other link).
textes.Écartelé de six : Aragon, Autriche, Farn: Quarterly of six: Aragon, Austria, Farnese, Medici, Burgundy, Brabant; Castile-León overall.
textes.Charles III est le fils d'Élisabeth Farn: Charles III is the son of Elisabeth Farnese: in 1761 he had the arms quartered of six, including that of Farnese.
textes.La page dit que le quartier de Médicis e: The page says the quarter of Medici also enters, without saying how.
textes.Les armes d'avant septembre 1868 revienn: The arms from before September 1868 return, with the escutcheon of Anjou without a bordure.
textes.Un décret du 8 janvier 1875 rétablit les: A decree of 8 January 1875 restored the arms from before September 1868; on the death of the Count of Chambord (1883), Alfonso XII bore the arms of France undifferenced.
textes.Les armes actuelles, avec l'écusson d'An: The present arms, with the oval escutcheon of Anjou overall.
textes.La loi 33/1981 remplace les armes de 197: Law 33/1981 replaced the arms of 1977; they were adopted following the democratic transition that took Spain out of Francoism.
textes.Les lis de France sont écartelés avec le: The lilies of France are quartered with the lions, in the place of honour.
textes.En 1328, Édouard III, petit-fils de Phil: In 1328 Edward III, grandson of Philip the Fair through his mother Isabella, was set aside: it was doubted that a woman could pass on a right she could not exercise, and the peers refused a foreign king. In 1337 he had a message sent to “Philip of Valois, who calls himself King of France”, breaking his homage: this was the start of the Hundred Years' War. In 1340 he took the lilies into his arms.
textes.Les lis du premier quartier sont les arm: The lilies of the first quarter are the arms of France (semé of lilies or).
textes.Ce sont les armes du royaume que le roi: These are the arms of the kingdom the King of England claims.
textes.Les armes prêtées à Édouard le Confesseu: The arms credited to Edward the Confessor are impaled with those of the King.
textes.Richard II accole à ses armes celles prê: Richard II impaled his arms with those credited to Edward the Confessor, as a sign of mystical union.
textes.Les armes du Confesseur sont abandonnées: The Confessor's arms are abandoned; the semé of France is reduced to three lilies.
textes.Henri IV abandonne les armes du Confesse: Henry IV abandoned the Confessor's arms and reduced the semé to three lilies, in imitation of Charles V of France.
textes.Les trois lis d'Angleterre copient les t: The three lilies of England copy the three lilies of France (1376).
textes.Charles V avait réduit le semé de France: Charles V had reduced the semé of France to three lilies in 1376; Henry IV of England imitated him.
textes.Les armes d'Angleterre sont accolées à c: The arms of England are impaled with those of Philip of Spain.
textes.Marie Ire accole les armes de son époux: Mary I impaled the arms of her Spanish husband.
textes.Les armes de Philippe, monarque espagnol: The arms of Philip, Spanish monarch, pass into the impaled shield.
textes.Les armes d'Écosse sont accolées à celle: The arms of Scotland are impaled with those of the Dauphin Francis.
textes.Au mariage de Marie avec le dauphin, les: On Mary's marriage to the Dauphin, the arms of Scotland were impaled with those of Francis, whose own shield as Dauphin brought them in as a quarter to mark his title of king consort.
textes.Les armes de France entrent dans l'écu d: The arms of France enter the shield of the Dauphin, impaled with Mary's.
textes.C'est le mari de Marie, François, dauphi: This is Mary's husband, Francis, Dauphin of France.
textes.Les armes d'Écosse sont accolées à celle: The arms of Scotland are impaled with those of France (dimidiated).
textes.Les armes de France, accolées (dimidiées: The arms of France, impaled (dimidiated), join the lion of Scotland.
textes.Le mari de Marie Stuart, François, devie: Mary Stuart's husband, Francis, became King of France in 1559.
textes.L'accolement est conservé, avec une légè: The impalement is kept, with a slight change.
textes.Le lion d'Écosse, la harpe d'Irlande et: The lion of Scotland, the harp of Ireland and the arms of England share a quartered shield.
textes.La reine Élisabeth Ire est morte sans en: Queen Elizabeth I died childless: James VI of Scotland, both of whose parents descended from Henry VII through Margaret Tudor, was her most likely heir. Proclaimed king in London on 24 March 1603, he united the crowns of Scotland, England and Ireland: the lion of Scotland, the harp of Ireland and the arms of England henceforth shared the shield.
textes.Les armes d'Angleterre, déjà chargées de: The arms of England, already charged with France, appear in them as a counter-quartering.
textes.Élisabeth Ire, dernière des Tudor, est m: Elizabeth I, last of the Tudors, died childless: the crown passed to the King of Scots, the most likely heir (see the other link).
textes.Les armes de 1603 reviennent avec Charle: The arms of 1603 return with Charles II.
textes.Elles ne servent pas pendant le Commonwe: They were not used during the Commonwealth: the monarchy had been abolished in 1649, and its arms with it.
textes.Parti : à dextre les armes de 1603 charg: Per pale: dexter, the arms of 1603 charged with the escutcheon of Nassau; sinister, the same without the escutcheon.
textes.Guillaume III et Marie II règnent ensemb: William III and Mary II reigned together and impaled their arms, identical except that William bore at the centre the escutcheon of his house, Nassau.
textes.Guillaume porte seul les armes de 1603,: William alone bears the arms of 1603, charged with the escutcheon of Nassau.
textes.Angleterre et Écosse partagent désormais: England and Scotland now share the same quarters.
textes.Les Actes d'Union fondent le royaume de: The Acts of Union founded the Kingdom of Great Britain: the title of King of Scots disappeared and the arms of the two kingdoms shared the same shield.
textes.Le Hanovre entre au quatrième quartier ;: Hanover enters the fourth quarter; “Dieu et mon droit” becomes the fixed motto.
textes.L'Acte d'établissement de 1701 désigne l: The Act of Settlement of 1701 named Electress Sophia of Hanover, the closest Protestant relative of the royal family, to succeed Queen Anne; fifty-six Catholics with better claims by blood were excluded. Sophia died on 8 June 1714, two months before Anne: her son George, Elector of Hanover, became direct heir, then was proclaimed king on 1 August. He brought his German lands into the fourth quarter.
textes.Les lis de France quittent l'écu ; l'Irl: The lilies of France leave the shield; Ireland takes its rank with England and Scotland; Hanover moves overall.
textes.L'Irlande est unie à la Grande-Bretagne: Ireland was united with Great Britain: by the proclamation of 1 January 1801, the King no longer called himself King of France and the lilies disappeared from the arms after more than four and a half centuries; the claim was abandoned the following year.
textes.Une couronne remplace le bonnet électora: A crown replaces the electoral bonnet on the escutcheon of Hanover.
textes.L'écusson de Hanovre quitte les armes, q: The escutcheon of Hanover leaves the arms, which take their present form.
textes.Victoria, exclue du trône de Hanovre par: Victoria, excluded from the throne of Hanover by Salic law, removed its escutcheon.
textes.Une bordure de gueules chargée de châtea: A bordure gules charged with castles or surrounds the shield of Portugal.
textes.Alphonse III monte sur le trône avec les: Alfonso III came to the throne with the arms he had taken as a younger son: the castles of the bordure are borrowed from his mother, a Castilian.
textes.Écartelé : aux 1 et 4 Castille et León,: Quarterly: 1 and 4, Castile and León; 2 and 3, Portugal.
textes.Pendant la crise de 1383-1385, Béatrice: During the crisis of 1383-1385, Beatrice bore the arms of Portugal in the 2nd and 3rd quarters, with those of her husband John I of Castile in the 1st and 4th.
textes.Les armes de Castille et León, celles de: The arms of Castile and León, her husband's, take up the first and fourth quarters.
textes.Béatrice est l'épouse de Jean Ier de Cas: Beatrice is the wife of John I of Castile: her arms bear those of her husband.
textes.La croix de l'ordre d'Aviz s'ajoute à l': The cross of the Order of Aviz is added to the shield.
textes.Jean d'Aviz, acclamé roi en 1385, ajoute: John of Aviz, acclaimed king in 1385, added the cross of his order to the shield.
textes.Écartelé : aux 1 et 4 Portugal, aux 2 et: Quarterly: 1 and 4, Portugal; 2 and 3, Castile and León.
textes.Les armes de Castille et León occupent l: The arms of Castile and León take up the second and third quarters.
textes.Ce sont les armes du royaume que revendi: These are the arms of the kingdom Alfonso V claims.
textes.La croix d'Aviz disparaît ; les écus son: The cross of Aviz disappears; the shields are set upright; five bezants in saltire.
textes.Jean II fait corriger ce qu'il tient pou: John II had corrected what he regarded as errors: the cross of Aviz disappeared, the dexter and sinister shields were set upright (lying down, they might have been taken for a mark of bastardy) and the bezants were fixed at five in saltire.
textes.Le chapeau rouge et les glands de cardin: The red hat and tassels of a cardinal top the royal crown.
textes.Les armes de Portugal passent dans l'écu: The arms of Portugal pass into the shield of the Spanish monarchy.
textes.L'écu de Portugal est posé sur la sphère: The shield of Portugal is set on the armillary sphere or on a field azure.
textes.Le Brésil est élevé au rang de royaume d: Brazil was raised to a kingdom within the United Kingdom of Portugal, Brazil and the Algarves: the shield of Portugal (for Portugal and the Algarves) was set on the armillary sphere, the arms of Brazil.
textes.La sphère armillaire, emblème du Brésil,: The armillary sphere, the emblem of Brazil, reappears in the arms of Orléans-Braganza.
