textes.Isabelle, héritière de l'empire du Brési: Isabel, heiress to the Empire of Brazil, married Gaston of Orléans: their descendants kept the Brazilian emblem and set the shield of Orléans at its centre.
textes.La croix blanche sur gueules remplace l': The white cross on gules replaces the black eagle (the two alternate at first).
textes.Pierre II, devenu comte, alterne l'aigle: Peter II, having become count, alternated the eagle and the cross. The cross is said to come from the emblem of the English crusaders, with whom he had taken the cross in 1250-1251.
textes.La croix est écartelée avec Saxe, Westph: The cross is quartered with Saxony, Westphalia, Engern, Chablais and Aosta.
textes.Emmanuel-Philibert vient de recouvrer se: Emmanuel Philibert had just recovered his States: he quartered the cross with the arms of these lands and surrounded the shield with the collar of the Order.
textes.Chypre, Jérusalem (avec Lusignan), Genèv: Cyprus, Jerusalem (with Lusignan), Geneva and Montferrat enter the shield, under a pavilion.
textes.Victor-Amédée Ier prétend aux couronnes: Victor Amadeus I claimed the crowns of Cyprus and Jerusalem: he brought their arms into the shield.
textes.Nice et Saluces entrent dans l'écu ; l'a: Nice and Saluzzo enter the shield; the eagle of Sicily, charged with Savoy, takes its centre.
textes.Par les traités d'Utrecht, Victor-Amédée: By the Treaties of Utrecht, Victor Amadeus II became King of Sicily.
textes.L'aigle passe sur champ d'or ; l'écu de: The eagle moves to a field or; the shield of Sardinia with the four Moor's heads is added.
textes.La Sicile est échangée contre la Sardaig: Sicily was exchanged for Sardinia: the arms of Sardinia entered the shield.
textes.La croix rouge de Gênes entre dans l'écu: The red cross of Genoa enters the simplified shield.
textes.Victor-Emmanuel Ier reçoit Gênes en 1815: Victor Emmanuel I received Genoa in 1815 and took the occasion to simplify his arms.
textes.Les armes de 1720, augmentées de Gênes,: The arms of 1720, augmented with Genoa, Nice, Piedmont and Saluzzo; overall the eagle, then the cross of Savoy.
textes.Les sources lues ne disent pas comment l: The sources read do not say how the crown passed to the Carignano branch.
textes.Le royaume d'Italie garde les armes d'or: The Kingdom of Italy keeps the original arms: gules, a cross argent.
textes.Dès 1831, Charles-Albert préfère en usag: From 1831 Charles Albert in practice preferred the small shield with the cross alone; the new kingdom kept the original arms.
textes.Les armes d'Espagne portent en abîme un: The arms of Spain bear at the fess point an escutcheon of Savoy.
textes.Le gouvernement provisoire de 1868 avait: The provisional government of 1868 had adopted the present territorial arms under a mural crown; Amadeo restored the royal crown and set an escutcheon of Savoy at the fess point.
textes.La ligne walramienne place une couronne: The Walramian line sets a crown on the lion of Nassau, which the first counts bore uncrowned.
textes.Les pages lues datent le partage de la m: The pages read date the division of the house (1251 or 1255 depending on the page) but do not say why the Walramian line adds a crown to the lion.
textes.La page « Maison de Nassau » date la div: The page “Maison de Nassau” dates the division to 1251 (death of Henry II); the page “Nassau-Dillenbourg” says “after 1255”.
textes.L'écu de la ligne ottonienne, d'abord ce: The shield of the Ottonian line, at first that of the Counts of Nassau, becomes a quartering: Nassau, Katzenelnbogen, Vianden, Diez.
textes.La ligne ottonienne se sépare en 1303 en: The Ottonian line split in 1303 into Nassau-Hadamar, Nassau-Siegen and Nassau-Dillenburg. The quarters then entered in stages: Diez by the marriage of Adolf to Jutta of Dietz (1386), Vianden recovered in 1420, and, after a succession dispute opened in 1500 and closed in 1557, the right to bear the title Count of Katzenelnbogen (most of the county going to Hesse).
textes.L'armorial donne le même écartelé à Otho: The armorial gives the same quartering to Otto II (died 1350) and to William the Rich (1487-1559), while the page “Nassau-Dillenbourg” places the arrival of Diez in 1386, Vianden in 1420 and the title of Katzenelnbogen in 1557: the blazon cannot be that of Otto II.
textes.Sur l'écartelé de Nassau-Dillenbourg vie: On the quartering of Nassau-Dillenburg comes a central escutcheon quarterly Châlon and Orange, itself charged with the escutcheon of Geneva.
textes.René de Nassau, dit René de Chalon, avai: René of Nassau, known as René of Chalon, had received the Principality of Orange in 1530 under the will (1528) of Philibert of Chalon, and had taken up its name and arms. Dying without issue at the siege of Saint-Dizier in July 1544, he made his cousin William his heir, notably for the Principality of Orange, on condition that he be brought up in the Catholic faith and live at Breda Castle.
textes.La page « Maison de Nassau » écrit que l: The page “Maison de Nassau” says the Ottonian line inherited the Principality of Orange in 1530; it was René (of the Breda branch) who received it in 1530, and William only in 1544.
textes.Deux écussons sont ajoutés en chef et en: Two escutcheons are added in chief and in base: the Marquisate of Veere and Flushing, and Buren.
textes.Le marquisat de Veere et Flessingue, pro: The Marquisate of Veere and Flushing, property of Philip II since 1567, was put up for sale by order of the Court of Holland in 1580; William bought it, which gave him two more votes in the States of Zeeland and a dominant position in that province. The armorial reports (citing a 1988 work on the stadtholders) that he then added to his arms the shield of Veere and of Buren. Buren came from his first marriage (1551) to Anna of Egmond, daughter and heiress of the Count of Buren.
textes.Le texte cité par l'armorial date l'adjo: The text cited by the armorial dates the addition to 1582; the page on William I places the entry of Buren into his family in 1551, without saying when the quarter appeared on the shield.
textes.La branche de Nassau-Dietz conserve l'éc: The Nassau-Dietz branch keeps the quartering of Nassau, Katzenelnbogen, Vianden, Diez and adds two quarters: Spiegelberg and Liesveld, with a cross of the Teutonic Order overall.
textes.À la mort de Jean VI de Nassau-Dillenbou: On the death of John VI of Nassau-Dillenburg in 1606, the county was divided into five counties, including Nassau-Dietz.
textes.Les pages lues ne disent pas comment Spi: The pages read do not say how Spiegelberg and Liesveld entered the shield of Nassau-Dietz.
textes.Les armes de Nassau-Dietz reprennent l'é: The arms of Nassau-Dietz take up the central escutcheon of Châlon-Orange with Geneva, Moers and Breda: the Frisian branch now bears the arms of the line of Orange.
textes.Guillaume III meurt le 8 mars 1702 et la: William III died on 8 March 1702 and the direct legitimate line of William the Silent died out. John William Friso of Nassau-Dietz, descended from a younger brother of William I and grandson of a sister of William II, inherited the Principality of Orange according to William III's wishes; Prussia also claimed the succession, through the union of Louise Henriette of Orange with Frederick William of Brandenburg.
textes.Le lion de Nassau sur champ billeté pren: The lion of Nassau on a billety field takes the crown, sword and sheaf of arrows of the States General.
textes.Les armes sont composées en 1815, après: The arms were composed in 1815, after the creation of the United Kingdom of the Netherlands by the Congress of Vienna: they combine the lion of Nassau on a field semé of billets with the crowned lion with sword and sheaf of arrows that appeared on the seal of the States General of the United Provinces.
textes.La page lue ne détaille pas ici la filia: The page read does not detail here the descent from the Nassau-Dietz to the first king.
textes.Les armes d'Orange passent aux Nassau-Di: The arms of Orange pass to the Nassau-Dietz, with Moers and Breda.
textes.Guillaume III meurt le 8 mars 1702 et la: William III died on 8 March 1702 and the direct line of William the Silent died out: John William Friso of Nassau-Dietz inherited the Principality of Orange according to his wishes.
textes.Le lion de Luxembourg (burelé) porte en: The lion of Luxembourg (barry) bears in surtout the escutcheon of Nassau.
textes.En 1890, Wilhelmine hérite du trône des: In 1890 Wilhelmina inherited the throne of the Netherlands but, under the treaty of 1783-1815 between the branches of the House of Nassau, which reserves the crown for male heirs alone, she was excluded from the Luxembourg succession: Adolf, heir of the senior branch, became Grand Duke.
textes.Les armes de Nassau et de Luxembourg fig: The arms of Nassau and Luxembourg appear in quarters II and III and at the centre.
textes.Les pages lues ne détaillent pas la succ: The pages read do not detail the succession between 1905 and 1919.
textes.Charlotte succède en 1919 à sa sœur aîné: Charlotte succeeded in 1919 her elder sister Marie-Adélaïde, who abdicated on 15 January 1919.
textes.L'écusson de la maison de Nassau entre e: The escutcheon of the House of Nassau enters at the centre of William's arms.
textes.Guillaume III d'Orange-Nassau et Marie I: William III of Orange-Nassau and Mary II impaled their arms; William's bear at the centre the escutcheon of his house, Nassau.
textes.Les deux fasces d'Oldenbourg occupent le: The two fesses of Oldenburg take up quarters 1 and 4; Delmenhorst quarters 2 and 3.
textes.La page lue sur Thierry ne dit pas comme: The page read on Dietrich does not say how Delmenhorst joined Oldenburg (see the next passage).
textes.Thierry, fils de Christian V d'Oldenbour: Dietrich, son of Christian V of Oldenburg, succeeded his father in 1423; he was Count of Oldenburg from 1423 to 1440.
textes.La croix pattée au pied fiché d'or sur a: The cross pattée with a fitched foot or on azure of Delmenhorst enters the shield, in quarters 2 and 3.
textes.Thierry est dit comte d'Oldenbourg et de: Dietrich is called Count of Oldenburg and Delmenhorst from 1423 to 1440: two counties brought together under one count, and the shield quarters them. In 1401 Dietrich had married Adelaide, daughter of Count Otto IV of Oldenburg-Delmenhorst (the page read does not say whether this marriage founds the union).
textes.Le Danebrog (croix pattée d'argent bordé: The Dannebrog (cross pattée argent fimbriated gules) divides the arms of Denmark, Sweden Modern, Norway Ancient and the Vandals; Schleswig and Holstein move overall, Oldenburg over all of that.
textes.Christian est comte d'Oldenbourg de 1440: Christian was Count of Oldenburg from 1440 to 1449, then King of Denmark (1448-1481), Norway (1450-1481) and Sweden (1457-1464): with each crown, one more shield, and the arms of the house retreat to the centre.
textes.La page lue ne dit ni sa filiation avec: The page read gives neither his descent from Dietrich nor the circumstances of his accessions.
textes.Les trois couronnes de Suède moderne res: The three crowns of Sweden Modern stay in the shield (quarter III), with the Goths in quarter IV and Stormarn overall; the lion of Norway moves to quarter II.
textes.La page ne lui donne que les couronnes d: The page gives him only the crowns of Denmark and Norway (1534-1559) and the Duchies of Holstein and Schleswig (1523-1533): his titles as read do not include Sweden, which his shield nevertheless cites.
textes.La page lue ne dit pas que ces quartiers: The page read does not say these quarters are a claim; it only shows that the titles cited do not include Sweden.
textes.L'écu s'étoffe : Goths et Vandales ont c: The shield fills out: Goths and Vandals each have a quarter, Gotland Ancient (the Paschal Lamb) enters the shield, Schleswig and Holstein are pushed further away; at least eight quarters around the Dannebrog.
textes.Frédéric II, fils de Christian III, est: Frederick II, son of Christian III, was King of Denmark and Norway from 1 January 1559.
textes.Même écu que celui de la période 1559-16: Same shield as in the period 1559-1699.
textes.La page lue ne consacre pas de ligne à F: The page read gives Frederick III no line; the figure is that of the period, and his place in the succession comes from the page on his son George.
textes.Suède moderne et Schleswig partagent le: Sweden Modern and Schleswig share quarter III (per fess), Goths and Vandals quarter IV; Holstein and Stormarn move overall.
textes.Frédéric IV, fils du roi précédent et de: Frederick IV, son of the previous king and Charlotte Amalie of Hesse-Kassel, succeeded his father on 25 August 1699.
textes.Le lion de Norvège (quartier II) dispara: The lion of Norway (quarter II) disappears from the shield; the Faroes and Greenland, which stay with the King, enter quarter III with the three crowns of Sweden Modern.
textes.Frédéric VI est roi de Danemark (1808-18: Frederick VI was King of Denmark (1808-1839) and of Norway from 1808 to 1814 only: the shield of the period 1819-1903 no longer bears Norway.
textes.La page lue ne nomme pas l'acte par lequ: The page read does not name the act by which Norway left the King of Denmark.
textes.L'Islande ancienne (la morue couronnée): Iceland Ancient (the crowned cod) is added to quarter III, beside the Faroes and Greenland.
textes.Christian IX est roi de Danemark de 1863: Christian IX was King of Denmark from 1863 to 1906 and the page places his shield in the branch of Schleswig-Holstein-Sonderburg-Glücksburg; the cod of Iceland is new compared with Frederick VI.
textes.La page lue ne dit pas comment la couron: The page read does not say how the crown came to him after Frederick VI.
textes.L'aigle d'argent de l'Islande moderne re: The eagle argent of Iceland Modern replaces the cod of Iceland Ancient.
textes.Christian X est roi de Danemark (1912-19: Christian X was King of Denmark (1912-1947) and of Iceland (1918-1944): the shield cites Iceland Modern.
textes.Le Danebrog est simplifié (croix d'argen: The Dannebrog is simplified (cross argent fimbriated gules) and divides the arms of Denmark in quarters 1 and 4; Iceland no longer appears; the Faroes and Greenland remain; Oldenburg alone overall.
textes.Christian X n'est roi d'Islande que jusq: Christian X was King of Iceland only until 1944 according to the page: the shield of the Queen, in power since 1972, no longer cites Iceland.
textes.La page lue ne détaille pas la successio: The page read does not detail the succession between Christian X and Margrethe II.
textes.Le lion d'or surmonté de trois étoiles d: The lion or surmounted by three stars of Monpezat takes up quarters 2 and 3, beside those of Denmark (1 and 4).
textes.Henri de Laborde de Monpezat est prince: Henri de Laborde de Monpezat was prince consort of Denmark from 1972 to 2016; his arms quarter those of Denmark with those of his family of origin.
textes.Plus de Danebrog, de trois couronnes ni: No more Dannebrog, three crowns or Goths: the shield keeps Norway, Schleswig, Holstein, Stormarn and Dithmarschen, with Oldenburg and Delmenhorst overall.
textes.Adolphe est duc de Schleswig et duc de S: Adolf was Duke of Schleswig and Duke of Schleswig-Holstein-Gottorp from 1544 to 1586; the page places him in the “Branche de (Oldenbourg)-Schleswig-Holstein-Gottorp”, a branch from the House of Oldenburg.
textes.La page lue ne dit pas son lien exact av: The page read does not state his exact link to Christian III.
textes.La croix de saint Éric d'or cantonne Suè: The cross of Saint Eric or divides Sweden Modern (1 and 4) and Sweden Ancient (2 and 3); the shield of Holstein-Gottorp moves overall.
textes.Adolphe-Frédéric est prince-évêque de Lü: Adolf Frederick was Prince-Bishop of Lübeck (1727-1750) then King of Sweden (1751-1771): a crown changing house is set down with the arms of the new one.
textes.La page lue ne dit pas pourquoi la Suède: The page read does not say why Sweden turned to him.
textes.Un pairle pattée d'or cantonne Suède mod: A pall pattée or divides Sweden Modern (in chief), Norway (to dexter: the lion with the halberd) and Sweden Ancient (to sinister); Holstein-Gottorp stays overall.
textes.Charles XIII est roi de Suède et, de 181: Charles XIII was King of Sweden and, from 1814 to 1818, King of Norway: the arms of Norway entered his shield at the very moment they left those of the King of Denmark.
textes.La page lue ne détaille pas le traité de: The page read does not detail the treaty of 1814.
textes.Le lion de Norvège quitte l'écu du roi d: The lion of Norway leaves the shield of the King of Denmark for that of the King of Sweden (it now holds a halberd).
textes.Frédéric VI est roi de Norvège de 1808 à: Frederick VI was King of Norway from 1808 to 1814; Charles XIII succeeded him as King of Norway in 1814 (pages read).
textes.L'aigle bicéphale de Russie (écusson de: The double-headed eagle of Russia (escutcheon of Saint George at the centre) is impaled with the arms of Holstein-Gottorp: Norway, Holstein, Stormarn, Dithmarschen, Oldenburg, Delmenhorst, Schleswig overall.
textes.Charles Pierre Ulrich est duc de Holstei: Charles Peter Ulrich was Duke of Holstein-Gottorp (1739-1762) and Emperor of Russia; the page places him in the “Rameau Schleswig-Holstein-Gottorp-Russie, dit Romanov”.
textes.La page lue ne dit pas comment la couron: The page read does not say how the crown of Russia came to him.
textes.Les armes de Holstein-Gottorp disparaiss: The arms of Holstein-Gottorp disappear from the shield: the double-headed eagle or remains alone, with Saint George at the centre.
textes.Alexandre II, dit le Libérateur, est dit: Alexander II, known as the Liberator, is called “Romanov-Holstein-Gottorp”; he was Emperor of Russia, Grand Duke of Finland and King of Poland from 1855 to 1881.
textes.La page lue ne détaille pas les passages: The page read does not detail the passages between Peter III and Alexander II.
textes.L'écu est parti : à dextre l'écartelé de: The shield is per pale: dexter, the quartering of Leuchtenberg, Eichstätt and Beauharnais; sinister, the imperial eagle of Russia.
textes.Maria Nikolaïevna est sœur d'Alexandre I: Maria Nikolaevna is the sister of Alexander II, Duchess of Leuchtenberg and Princess of Eichstätt: the impalement gives her husband's arms to dexter, those of her birth to sinister.
The page read does not name the husband.
textes.Armes alternatives : flèche et ancre en: Alternative arms: arrow and anchor in saltire under a star, bordure charged with eight roses; two anchors in saltire behind the shield.
textes.Frère d'Alexandre II et amiral, Constant: Brother of Alexander II and an admiral, Constantine bears “the arms of the Emperor's younger brothers and sons” with two anchors behind the shield; his motto, “droit et vrai”, translates the Saxon “Treu und Glauben”, in homage to his wife Alexandra of Saxe-Altenburg.
textes.Armes alternatives : deux haches passées: Alternative arms: two axes in saltire within a wreath of roses, bordure sable with eight lion's heads; two axes behind the shield.
textes.Frère d'Alexandre II et inspecteur génér: Brother of Alexander II and Inspector General of military engineering, Nicholas bears the same arms of the Emperor's younger brothers and sons, with two axes for his office.
textes.Armes alternatives : le griffon de Roman: Alternative arms: the griffin of Romanov holding a round shield with the bend of Baden, bordure sable with eight lion's heads; two cannons behind the shield.
textes.Frère d'Alexandre II et maréchal, Michel: Brother of Alexander II and a field marshal, Michael bears the arms of the Romanovs with the bend of the House of Baden on the round shield, in homage to his wife Cecily of Baden; two cannons behind the shield.
textes.Sur une croix alésée d'argent (Grèce) su: On a cross couped argent (Greece) on azure, a simplified escutcheon of Glücksburg: Dannebrog, Denmark, Schleswig, Holstein, Lauenburg, and Oldenburg-Delmenhorst overall.
textes.Georges est dit de Schleswig-Holstein-So: George is called of Schleswig-Holstein-Sonderburg-Glücksburg and King of the Hellenes (1863-1913): the armorial places him in the same Glücksburg branch as Christian IX.
textes.La page lue ne dit pas comment la couron: The page read does not say how the crown of Greece came to him.
textes.L'écusson central devient l'écu complet: The central escutcheon becomes the complete shield of Denmark (Sweden Modern, the Faroes, Greenland, Iceland Ancient, Goths, Vandals, Holstein, Lauenburg…) instead of the simplified version.
textes.Constantin (1913-1917), Alexandre (1917-: Constantine (1913-1917), Alexander (1917-1920) then George II (1922-1924, 1935-1947) bear the arms after George I; those of George II are the ones after 1936.
textes.À senestre, l'écartelé de Grèce (croix a: To sinister, the quartering of Greece (cross couped) with the escutcheon of Denmark overall: her arms of birth.
textes.Sofía est dite princesse de Grèce et de: Sofía is called Princess of Greece and Denmark: her shield takes up the arms of the royal house of Greece.
textes.La page lue ne dit pas de quel roi des H: The page read does not say from which King of the Hellenes she descends.
textes.À dextre, l'écartelé de Castille, León,: To dexter, the quartering of Castile, León, Aragon, Navarre and Granada, with the escutcheon of Anjou; the arms of Greece and Denmark move to sinister.
textes.Princesse d'Espagne puis reine consort d: Princess of Spain then queen consort of Spain from 1975 (page read): her shield is per pale, her husband's Spain to dexter.
textes.Au second parti : Danebrog écartelé (Dan: In the second part: the Dannebrog quartered (Denmark, Schleswig, Sweden Modern, Iceland Ancient, the Faroes, Greenland, Goths, Vandals) and Holstein, Stormarn, Dithmarschen, Lauenburg; Oldenburg and Delmenhorst over all of that.
textes.Alexandra est princesse de Danemark : so: Alexandra is a Princess of Denmark: her shield bears, in the second part, the full arms of Denmark of the time.
The page read does not name her father.
textes.Le royaume de son époux, Édouard VII, oc: The kingdom of her husband, Edward VII, takes up the first part: England in quarters 1 and 4, Scotland in 2, Ireland in 3.
textes.Alexandra est reine du Royaume-Uni en ta: Alexandra was Queen of the United Kingdom as the wife of Edward VII (1901-1910): to dexter, the King's arms.
textes.Écartelé : Danemark (I), Grèce (II), Mou: Quarterly: Denmark (I), Greece (II), Mountbatten-Battenberg (III), Edinburgh (IV, a castle); the arms of 1947-1949, judged “unsatisfactory”, were replaced.
textes.Philippe de Grèce et de Danemark, dit Mo: Philip of Greece and Denmark, known as Mountbatten, was prince consort of Elizabeth II; the armorial gives as his arms after 1949 a quartering recalling his birth, his new family and his title.
textes.La page lue ne détaille pas ses ascendan: The page read does not detail his Greek ancestors.
textes.L'écu ne garde que le lion de Norvège co: The shield keeps only the crowned lion of Norway holding the axe: no more Dannebrog, Schleswig or Oldenburg.
textes.Christian Frédéric Charles Georges Walde: Christian Frederik Carl Georg Valdemar Axel of Schleswig-Holstein-Sonderburg-Glücksburg became King of Norway (1905-1957) as Haakon VII: the page places him in the Glücksburg branch, but his arms keep only those of the kingdom.
textes.La page lue ne dit pas comment il a été: The page read does not say how he was chosen or his exact link to Christian IX.
textes.Les armes du Danemark brisées d'un lambe: The arms of Denmark differenced by a label argent with each point bearing three ermine spots sable.
textes.Georges est fils du roi Frédéric III (pa: George is the son of King Frederick III (page “Georges de Danemark”); the armorial gives him the King's shield with a label, the cadet's mark.
textes.La page lue ne dit pas pourquoi les pend: The page read does not say why the points bear ermine spots.
textes.Aucun quartier d'Angleterre n'entre dans: No quarter of England enters his shield: he stays armed as a Prince of Denmark, with the label; the English titles (Duke of Cumberland, Knight of the Garter, 1684) come beside it.
textes.Il épouse Anne le 28 juillet 1683 à Lond: He married Anne on 28 July 1683 in London, a British subject and prince consort of England, Scotland and Ireland from 1702 to 1708; the marriage, judging by his shield, added nothing to the husband's arms.
textes.L'écu royal (France contre-écartelé d'An: The royal shield (France quartering England, Scotland, Ireland) becomes the son's, with the Dannebrog overall and a label argent with the second point bearing the cross of Saint George.
textes.Guillaume, duc de Gloucester (1689-1700): William, Duke of Gloucester (1689-1700), was the only one of the children of George and Anne to survive infancy; he died at eleven. It is on the child's shield, not his father's, that the two kingdoms meet.
textes.Le lion de Misnie s'écartèle avec le lio: The lion of Meissen is quartered with the barry lion of Thuringia.
textes.Henri III est margrave de Misnie et de B: Henry III was Margrave of Meissen and Lower Lusatia, Landgrave of Thuringia and Count Palatine of Saxony (1247-1265): each title brings its shield.
textes.La page lue ne dit pas comment la Thurin: The page read does not say how Thuringia came to him.
textes.Le burelé de sable et d'or au crancelin: The barry sable and or with a crancelin vert becomes the shield of the electorate; a per fess sable and argent with two swords represents the Arch-Marshalship of the Empire.
textes.Frédéric est margrave de Misnie (1381-14: Frederick was Margrave of Meissen (1381-1423), then Elector of Saxony and Count Palatine of Saxony (1423-1428).
textes.La page lue ne dit pas comment l'élector: The page read does not say how the electorate came to him.
textes.L'électeur garde le burelé de Saxe et l': The Elector keeps the barry of Saxony and the Arch-Marshalship.
textes.À la mort de Frédéric II, ses fils divis: On the death of Frederick II, his sons divided his inheritance: the elder, Ernest, became Elector and received northern Meissen, southern Thuringia, Wittenberg and the electoral title.
textes.L'écu s'écartèle : le burelé de Saxe au: The shield is quartered: the barry of Saxony in I, Thuringia in II, the Palatinate of Saxony in III, Meissen in IV.
textes.Albert III, le cadet, devient duc et reç: Albert III, the younger, became Duke and received northern Thuringia and southern Meissen.
textes.Le burelé de Saxe n'est plus qu'un quart: The barry of Saxony is now only one quarter, among many others: Palatinate of Saxony, Thuringia, Meissen, Orlamünde, Pleissen, Engern, Landsberg, Palatinate of Thuringia…
textes.Jean-Frédéric est électeur de Saxe, comt: John Frederick was Elector of Saxony, Count Palatine of Saxony and Landgrave of Thuringia from 1532 to 1547, then deposed: he was afterwards Duke of Saxe-Weimar.
textes.Clèves, Juliers et Berg entrent dans l'é: Cleves, Jülich and Berg enter the shield, beside Thuringia, Meissen and the barry of Saxony.
textes.La page range Jean-Ernest (1658-1729) pa: The page places John Ernest (1658-1729) among the Dukes of Saxe-Saalfeld then of Saxe-Coburg-Saalfeld, in the Ernestine line.
textes.La page lue ne dit pas sa filiation ni c: The page read does not state his descent or how Cleves, Jülich and Berg entered the shield.
textes.Armes moyennes : Thuringe, Misnie, une p: Middle arms: Thuringia, Meissen, a hen sable on a mount, Vogtland, and the barry of Saxony overall.
textes.Ernest est duc de Saxe-Cobourg-Saalfeld: Ernest was Duke of Saxe-Coburg-Saalfeld (1806-1826), then of Saxe-Coburg-Gotha (1826-1844).
textes.La page lue ne dit pas sa filiation avec: The page read does not state his descent from John Ernest.
textes.Le burelé de Saxe reste aux quartiers II: The barry of Saxony stays in quarters II and III of the shield.
textes.La page range Albert, prince de Saxe-Cob: The page places Albert, Prince of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha and Duke in Saxony, in the “Rameau anglais de Saxe-Cobourg-Gotha”.
textes.Les trois royaumes (Angleterre, Écosse,: The three kingdoms (England, Scotland, Ireland) take up quarters I and IV, the barry of Saxony II and III, with a label argent of three points, the middle one bearing the cross of Saint George.
textes.Albert est prince consort de Grande-Bret: Albert was prince consort of Great Britain and Ireland after his marriage to Queen Victoria; Knight of the Garter in 1839.
textes.Les trois royaumes occupent les quatre q: The three kingdoms take up the four quarters, differenced by a label argent of three points; the barry of Saxony moves overall.
textes.Albert-Édouard est prince de Galles de 1: Albert Edward was Prince of Wales from 1841 to 1901, Duke of Saxe-Coburg-Gotha, then King of the United Kingdom as Edward VII.
textes.Même écu que son père, mais le lambel d': Same shield as his father, but the label argent has five points.
textes.Avant 1892, George est duc d'York, comte: Before 1892, George was Duke of York, Earl of Inverness and Baron Killarney; he became Prince of Wales (1901-1910), then King of the United Kingdom (1910-1936).
textes.Variante 1 : le royaume britannique aux: Variant 1: the British kingdom in quarters I and IV, Brunswick, Lüneburg and a rearing horse overall.
textes.Léopold est prince de Saxe-Cobourg et Go: Leopold, Prince of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha and Duke in Saxony, was elected King of the Belgians in 1831.
textes.La page lue ne dit pas sa filiation, ni: The page read does not state his descent, or why the British kingdom appears in this first variant (it gives several before the arms became fixed).
textes.Le lion d'or de Belgique porte en cœur l: The lion or of Belgium bears at the centre the barry escutcheon of Saxony.
textes.Léopold est duc de Brabant (1835-1865),: Leopold was Duke of Brabant (1835-1865), King of the Belgians (1865-1909) and sovereign of the Congo Free State (1884-1908).
textes.Les armes sont celles du Portugal ; le b: The arms are those of Portugal; the barry of Saxony of Ferdinand II does not appear.
textes.Pierre V (1837-1861) est fils de Marie I: Peter V (1837-1861) is the son of Maria II and Ferdinand II; Louis I, Charles I and Manuel II, overthrown by the revolution of 1910, bear the same arms.
textes.La page lue ne dit pas comment la couron: The page read does not say how the crown passed to the sons of Maria II.
textes.Le burelé de Saxe est mis en parti avec: The barry of Saxony is impaled with the arms of Portugal for the time of the king consort; his sons keep none of it.
textes.Ferdinand II (1816-1885) est roi consort: Ferdinand II (1816-1885) was king consort of Maria II from 1837 to 1853; he bore an impalement: 1, the arms of Portugal; 2, the barry of Saxony.
textes.Un lion d'or couronné sur gueules rempla: A crowned lion or on gules replaces the Saxon quarters.
textes.Ferdinand est prince régnant de Bulgarie: Ferdinand was reigning Prince of Bulgaria (1887-1908) and Governor General of Eastern Rumelia, then King of Bulgaria (1908-1918).
textes.La page lue ne dit ni sa filiation ni co: The page read states neither his descent nor how he was chosen.
textes.Une sphère armillaire d'or sur une croix: An armillary sphere or on a cross of the Order of Christ, surrounded by twenty stars, bears overall the barry of Saxony.
textes.La page range ces armes sous « Prétendan: The page places these arms under “Prétendants au trône brésilien de la dynastie de Saxe-Coburgo-Bragança”.
textes.La page lue ne donne ni la filiation ni: The page read gives neither the descent nor the date of the passage.
textes.La Pologne et la Hongrie (mi-parti) entr: Poland and Hungary (dimidiated) enter quarter III, Landsberg IV; the Arch-Marshalship moves overall.
textes.Jean-Georges est électeur de Saxe, comte: John George was Elector of Saxony, Count Palatine of Saxony and Margrave of Meissen from 1611 to 1656.
textes.La page lue ne dit pas pourquoi la Polog: The page read does not say why Poland and Hungary appear in the shield: it does not call him king of either.
textes.Les petites armes du royaume se réduisen: The lesser arms of the kingdom shrink to the barry of Saxony; the great arms take up Meissen, Thuringia and the two Palatinates.
textes.Frédéric-Auguste le Juste est électeur d: Frederick Augustus the Just was Elector of Saxony, then King of Saxony (1806-1827) and Duke of Warsaw (1807-1815).
textes.La page lue ne détaille pas la successio: The page read does not detail the succession between John George I and him.
textes.Le lion palatin (de sable au lion d'or c: The Palatine lion (sable, a lion or crowned gules) is quartered with the lozengy of Bavaria; the Elector adds the orb of the Arch-Steward overall.
textes.Otton l'Illustre reçoit le titre de comt: Otto the Illustrious received the title Count Palatine of the Rhine by his marriage to the heiress of the Welf Henry of Brunswick, a dignity carrying sovereignty over the Palatinate.
textes.L'aigle de sable sur or de l'Empire occu: The eagle sable on or of the Empire fills the shield; the Palatine lion and the lozengy of Bavaria move overall.
textes.Robert de Wittelsbach est roi des Romain: Rupert of Wittelsbach was King of the Romans from 1400 to 1410.
textes.La page lue ne dit pas comment il est él: The page read does not say how he was elected.
textes.Un parti de Bohême, de Moravie, de Silés: An impalement of Bohemia, Moravia, Silesia, Luxembourg and Upper Lusatia replaces the Palatine arms.
textes.Frédéric V est électeur palatin et archi: Frederick V was Elector Palatine and Arch-Steward from 1610 to 1623 and King of Bohemia from 1619 to 1620; he was defeated in 1620 after trying to take the Kingdom of Bohemia.
textes.Écartelé : le fuselé de Bavière aux 1 et: Quarterly: the lozengy of Bavaria in 1 and 4, the Palatine lion in 2 and 3, and overall the orb crossed or on gules.
textes.En 1620, l'électeur palatin Frédéric V,: In 1620 the Protestant Elector Palatine Frederick V was defeated; placed under the imperial ban, his lands, his electoral title and his office of Steward were confiscated and given to his Catholic cousin, the Duke of Bavaria, who then took this shield.
textes.Son titre d'électeur, ses terres et sa c: His electoral title, his lands and his office of Steward pass to the Duke of Bavaria.
textes.Même passage que ci-dessus, vu depuis le: The same passage as above, seen from the defeated side: he was placed under the imperial ban after his defeat of 1620.
textes.L'aigle de sable sur or occupe l'écu ; l: The eagle sable on or fills the shield; the lozengy of Bavaria and the Palatine lion are quartered, the orb crossed overall.
textes.Charles VII de Bavière est empereur de 1: Charles VII of Bavaria was Emperor from 1742 to 1745.
textes.La page lue ne dit pas comment l'électio: The page read does not say how the election took place.
textes.L'aigle de sable sur or de l'Empire reço: The eagle sable on or of the Empire receives the lozengy of Bavaria overall.
textes.Louis IV de Bavière est roi des Romains: Louis IV of Bavaria was King of the Romans in 1314, crowned Holy Roman Emperor in 1328; the page places him in the Ludovician branch, the junior one.
The page read does not state his descent.
textes.Le fuselé de Bavière est mis en parti av: The lozengy of Bavaria is impaled with the eagle gules of Brandenburg.
textes.Louis V (mort en 1361), Louis VI (mort e: Louis V (died 1361), Louis VI (died 1365) and Otto V (died 1379) were Dukes of Bavaria and Electors of Brandenburg.
textes.La page lue ne dit pas comment le Brande: The page read does not say how Brandenburg came to them.
textes.Le fuselé de Bavière est écartelé avec l: The lozengy of Bavaria is quartered with the lions of Hainault and Holland.
textes.La page lue les dit ducs de Bavière-Stra: The page read calls them Dukes of Bavaria-Straubing and Counts of Hainault and Holland, until 1433.
textes.La page lue ne dit pas comment Hainaut e: The page read does not say how Hainault and Holland came to them.
textes.Le parti palatin-Bavière reçoit sur le t: The Palatine-Bavaria impalement receives overall the lion of Veldenz; Jülich, Cleves, Berg and La Marck enter the second part.
textes.La page lue les dit comtes palatins de D: The page read calls them Counts Palatine of Zweibrücken from 1569 to 1675, in the Rudolphine branch.
textes.La page lue ne dit pas comment Juliers,: The page read does not say how Jülich, Cleves, Berg and La Marck entered the shield.
textes.La croix de saint Éric d'or cantonne la: The cross of Saint Eric or divides Sweden Modern and Sweden Ancient; Bavaria, Jülich, Cleves, Berg and other quarters move overall.
textes.La page lue les dit rois de Suède de 165: The page read calls them Kings of Sweden from 1654 to 1720, descended from the Counts Palatine of Zweibrücken.
textes.La page lue ne dit pas comment la couron: The page read does not say how the crown of Sweden came to them.
textes.Palatinat en Bavière, 1799-1804 : Julier: Palatinate in Bavaria, 1799-1804: Jülich, Berg, Cleves, Sponheim, Birkenfeld and other quarters in an impalement.
textes.Maximilien (1756-1825), duc de Deux-Pont: Maximilian (1756-1825), Duke of Zweibrücken and Count of Birkenfeld, became Elector Palatine and Elector of Bavaria (Maximilian IV), then first King of Bavaria.
textes.La page lue ne détaille pas comment les: The page read does not detail how the electorates came to him.
textes.Le fuselé de Bavière porte en cœur un éc: The lozengy of Bavaria bears at the centre an escutcheon gules with a sword and sceptre in saltire, under a royal crown.
textes.La page lue donne ces armes aux rois de: The page read gives these arms to the Kings of Bavaria from 1809 to 1835.
textes.La page lue ne dit pas comment la royaut: The page read does not say how the royal title was acquired.
textes.Le texte de la page dit 1809-1835 ; la f: The page's text says 1809-1835; the figure is dated 1806.
textes.Écartelé : Palatinat du Rhin, Franconie,: Quarterly: Palatinate of the Rhine, Franconia, Burgau, Veldenz, with the lozengy of Bavaria overall.
textes.La page lue donne cet écu aux rois de Ba: The page read gives this shield to the Kings of Bavaria from 1835 to 1918.
textes.La page lue ne dit pas pourquoi les arme: The page read does not say why the arms changed in 1835.
textes.Une croix alésée d'argent sur azur porte: A cross couped argent on azure bears the lozengy of Bavaria overall.
textes.Othon de Wittelsbach (1815-1867) est roi: Otto of Wittelsbach (1815-1867) was King of Greece; the figure is dated 1831 to 1863.
textes.La page lue ne dit pas sa filiation ni c: The page read does not state his descent or how he became king.
textes.Le fuselé de Bavière sur la croix alésée: The lozengy of Bavaria on the cross couped is replaced by the escutcheon of Glücksburg.
textes.La page de Wittelsbach donne Othon roi d: The Wittelsbach page gives Otto as King of Greece (figure from 1831 to 1863); the Oldenburg page gives George I as King of the Hellenes (1863-1913); neither says how one succeeded the other.
textes.Les mêmes alérions, brisés d'un lambel d: The same alerions, differenced by a label azure.
textes.Les comtes de Vaudémont sont une branche: The Counts of Vaudémont are a cadet branch of the House of Lorraine: the label azure marks their cadet status.
textes.Le lambel d'azur disparaît : l'écu redev: The label azure disappears: the shield becomes that of Lorraine again.
textes.Charles II (1364-1431) n'ayant pas de fi: As Charles II (1364-1431) had no son, his nephew Anthony of Vaudémont became head of the House of Lorraine and removed the label azure that marked his cadet status.
textes.Lorraine aux quartiers 1 et 4 ; Hongrie,: Lorraine in quarters 1 and 4; Hungary, Anjou-Sicily, Jerusalem, Anjou and Bar in 2 and 3.
textes.La page dit que ces armes combinent cell: The page says these arms combine those of both his parents; René II (1451-1508) used them until 1500.
textes.La page lue ne nomme pas ses parents ni: The page read names neither his parents nor his descent from Anthony.
textes.Hongrie, Anjou-Sicile, Jérusalem, Aragon: Hungary, Anjou-Sicily, Jerusalem, Aragon, Anjou and Bar form a per fess; Lorraine moves overall.
textes.La page donne cet écu aux ducs de Lorrai: The page gives this shield to the Dukes of Lorraine from René II, from 1500, until Anthony (1489-1544), around 1538.
textes.La page lue ne dit pas pourquoi les arme: The page read does not say why the arms changed in 1500.
textes.Gueldre (lion contourné) et Juliers (lio: Guelders (lion contourné) and Jülich (lion sable) enter the shield.
textes.Héritées de Philippe de Gueldre (1467-15: Inherited from Philippa of Guelders (1467-1544), Lorraine's claims to the Duchies of Guelders and Jülich went no further than this heraldic addition.
textes.Il reprend l'écu de la période d'Antoine: He took up the shield of the period from Anthony to Francis III; the page refers to the Habsburg-Lorraine for his descendants.
textes.François (1708-1765), anciennement Franç: Francis (1708-1765), formerly Francis III of Lorraine, was Grand Duke of Tuscany (Francis II); the page gives the shield of the period c. 1538-1737 to Francis III, in 1737.
textes.La page lue ne dit pas comment la Toscan: The page read does not say how Tuscany came to him.
textes.Bar et Toscane entrent dans le cœur de l: Bar and Tuscany enter the centre of the shield of the Habsburg-Lorraine (see that passage).
textes.La page de Lorraine ne détaille pas la d: The Lorraine page does not detail the descendants of Francis: it refers to the Habsburg-Lorraine part of the Armorial of the Habsburgs.
textes.Le lion de sable sur or de Flandre rempl: The lion sable on or of Flanders replaces the arms of Lorraine.
textes.Thierry d'Alsace (vers 1100-1168), fils: Thierry of Alsace (c. 1100-1168), younger son of Thierry II of Lorraine, inherited the County of Flanders through his mother Gertrude; his son Philip of Alsace adopted these lion arms, which became emblematic of Flanders.
textes.Les mêmes quartiers, brisés d'un lambel: The same quarters, differenced by a label gules, with Lorraine differenced in the same way overall.
textes.Claude II de Lorraine (1496-1550) est co: Claude II of Lorraine (1496-1550) was Count of Aumale, Count of Guise, Baron of Elbeuf, Mayenne and Joinville, then Duke of Guise and Peer of France.
textes.La page lue ne dit pas de quand date l'é: The page read does not say when the shield dates from or why the label is gules.
textes.L'écu lorrain est mi-parti avec la Franc: The Lorraine shield is dimidiated with France.
textes.La page range Louise de Lorraine (1553-1: The page places Louise of Lorraine (1553-1601), daughter of Nicholas, Duke of Mercœur, among the cadet branches of the house.
textes.La page lue ne dit pas par quel passage: The page read does not say by what passage the Mercœur connect to the Dukes of Lorraine of the previous period.
textes.L'écu est mi-parti : les trois lis de Fr: The shield is dimidiated: the three lilies of France to dexter, Lorraine to sinister.
textes.Louise de Lorraine est mariée en 1575 à: Louise of Lorraine married Henry III (1551-1589), King of France, in 1575.
